title: The Effect of Quantization on Clinical Benchmarks: Accuracy and Safety Across Model Families
abstract: Quantization enables deployment of large language models on resource-constrained clinical edge devices, but its effect on clinical accuracy and safety remains understudied. We evaluate five 7-8B parameter models at FP16, GPTQ-INT8, and GPTQ-INT4 precision across five benchmarks: MedQA, MedMCQA, Med-HALT, a risk-stratified sample of HealthBench, and MedSafetyBench. The study jointly varies quantization bit width, model family, and clinical task type, with explicit risk stratification and safety measures. INT8 GPTQ is universally safe (max. degradation -1.9%-1.9%), while INT4 degradation is substantial and model-dependent: BioMistral-7B, clinically fine-tuned, loses 19.7% on MedMCQA, more than any general-purpose model, showing clinical fine-tuning does not confer compression robustness. MedMCQA degrades more than MedQA under INT4; Med-HALT is largely unaffected. On HealthBench's emergency-risk subgroup, Qwen2.5-7B degrades by 26.8% under INT4, suggesting high-risk scenarios are disproportionately vulnerable to compression. On MedSafetyBench, the model family dominates over precision (refusal rates range 10.2%-74.9% at FP16), though Qwen2.5-7B (-17.8%) and Meditron-7B (-28.3%) show substantial INT4 safety degradation; notably, Qwen2.5-7B is simultaneously the most accuracy-robust model, demonstrating that accuracy and safety robustness are independent properties. We additionally test two recovery methods, clinical calibration substitution and QLoRA fine-tuning, both producing the same trade-off: MedMCQA recovers while MedQA further degrades, indicating recovery strategies require task-specific validation rather than being assumed universally beneficial. These findings indicate INT8 is broadly safe for clinical deployment, while INT4 safety must be assessed per-model and per-task, and that safety alignment is determined primarily by instruction tuning rather than clinical domain adaptation.

title: Where Reliability Lives: Experimental Localisation of Behavioural Properties in an Agent System
abstract: Reliability claims about agentic systems implicitly locate each property somewhere: in the model, or in the machinery around it. We built a system where that location is an experimental question. The subject is a persistent simulated settlement whose authoritative append-only ledger adjudicates every attempted act against world state; accepted history is the only reality. Mind, institution and world were separated before any experiment. Holding cognition fixed, we intervened on the institution's epistemic mechanisms (evidence provenance, belief availability, physical-evidence legibility); preregistered experiments refuted our central prediction twice, in opposite directions. A registered falsifier then supplied the input the geometry had denied the belief channel, a staged veridical first-hand witness, and its marginal value, non-positive throughout the witness-free phases, turned positive: 9 of 11 seeds, zero added false attribution. Holding institutional enforcement fixed, we intervened on cognition four ways: ablating the native minds' machinery, killing and resetting them mid-task, substituting a frozen frontier-LLM panel for the entire native cognition, and corrupting beliefs with trusted false testimony. Behaviour changed dramatically: one falsehood cost each trusting run about 900 futile actions and the distrusting arm none. Five pre-declared properties did not move in any tested trajectory: accepted reality stayed singular, invalid attempts were refused with typed reasons, duties outlived their processes, no work was accepted twice, and no false completion was ever accepted (2,581 substituted-panel claims, none false). Our claim is limited to this setting: measured behavioural properties were separable from substantial changes to cognition, established by intervention. One designed world, not a population of institutions; no test of an agent optimising against the institution.

title: Group-Aware Adaptive Retrieval for Evidence Navigation
abstract: Reasoning-intensive retrieval addresses queries whose relevance cannot be identified by surface-level matching, thereby requiring multi-step reasoning. Because relevant documents rarely appear in the initial candidate set, retrieval systems suffer from the bounded recall problem. Existing methods iteratively expand a candidate pool at the document level over a corpus graph, examining each neighbor in isolation and drifting toward a narrow region of the corpus. To address this problem, we propose Group-Aware Adaptive Retrieval for Evidence Navigation (GAREN), which explores the corpus graph through group-level expansion. GAREN organizes documents into semantically coherent and distinguishable groups based on their connections in the corpus graph. The information in each group indicates what can be accessed by expanding through it, providing guidance beyond individual document-level signals. At each iteration, GAREN uses a group-level navigator to identify promising expansion directions, retrieves documents from the selected groups, and applies a document-level reranker to evaluate the updated candidate set. Extensive experiments show that GAREN achieves up to 8.0% improvement over the strongest baseline on BRIGHT. The source code is available at https://github.com/KJ12124/GAREN

title: DynG-Diff: A State-Aware Dynamic Guidance Diffusion Framework for Probabilistic Time Series Forecasting
abstract: Probabilistic multivariate time series (MTS) forecasting is crucial for modeling complex dynamical systems. However, existing diffusion-based methods rely on task-specific conditional paradigms that lack flexibility and struggle with inherent "information heterogeneity"--the significantly varying noise levels and evolutionary patterns across variables. To address this, we propose DynG-Diff, a variable-sensitive dynamic guidance diffusion framework for probabilistic multivariate time-series forecasting: (1) DynG-Diff adopts a two-stage separated training strategy and uses an unconditional diffusion backbone to model the joint distribution of multivariate time series. (2) DynG-Diff introduces a lightweight state-aware policy network that adaptively infers variable reliability from real-time noisy states and one-step denoising estimates, outputting a dynamic guidance strength matrix. (3) DynG-Diff mathematically formulates this dynamic weight as the local precision of the observation distribution, enabling precise guidance for high-confidence variables during inference while filtering out interference from anomalous noise. Extensive experiments on real-world benchmarks demonstrate competitive probabilistic forecasting performance against state-of-the-art conditional diffusion models and improved robustness under severe observation corruption.The implementation code is available at: https://github.com/TT-20011031/DynG-Diff

title: A Multi-layer Linguistic Profiling Framework for Emotion Recognition in Text: A Data-Driven Natural Language Processing (NLP) Study Using the Kaggle Emotions Dataset
abstract: Background Emotion recognition in text underpins a wide range of human-centered artificial intelligence (AI) applications, yet existing frameworks either prioritize accuracy at the expense of interpretability or analyze emotional language through a single lens. This study developed and evaluated the Multi-layer Emotion Linguistic Profiling Framework (MELPF), a reproducible protocol integrating lexical, structural, and model-level interpretability analyses to characterize how emotional meaning is encoded in short text. Methods The Kaggle Emotions Dataset (16,000 training, 2,000 validations, and 2,000 test instances; six emotion categories) was used. The corpus exhibits pronounced class imbalance: joy (33.5%) and sadness (29.2%) dominate, while surprise is underrepresented (3.6%); in addition, all statistics were derived strictly from training instances to prevent data leakage. MELPF operates across five stages: preprocessing; lexical profiling (unigram/bigram distributions, term frequency-inverse document frequency {TF-IDF}, pointwise mutual information (PMI), and co-occurrence analysis); structural profiling (part-of-speech {POS} distribution and template identification); supervised classification using logistic regression, a linear support vector machine (SVM), random forest, a bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) network, and Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) (base-uncased variant); and cross-layer synthesis via feature-importance mapping and attention visualization. Results BERT achieved the highest macro-F1 (the macro-averaged F1 score, i.e., the harmonic mean of precision and recall; 0.92, accuracy 0.93), followed by BiLSTM (0.89), linear SVM (0.88), logistic regression (0.86), and random forest (0.81). Ablation confirmed that PMI-derived and POS-based features improved macro-F1 from 0.88 to 0.89 over the TF-IDF baseline. Lexical profiling identified category-discriminative unigrams and high-PMI bigrams, while structural profiling revealed a dominant first-person copular frame. Feature-importance scores and attention visualization confirmed alignment between salient tokens and model decisions. Conclusion MELPF offers a transparent, reproducible methodology for examining emotional meaning across multiple linguistic layers, bridging theoretical linguistics and applied NLP.

title: Implementasi Artificial Intelligence pada Customer Experience di Platform E-commerce di Indonesia: Literature Review
abstract: Penerapan teknologi Artificial Intelligence (AI) yang saat ini semakin masif di berbagai sektor memberikan pengaruh tersendiri. Salah satunya terkait customer experience pengguna platform e-commerce yang ada di Indonesia untuk sektor ekonomi. Saat ini telah banyak kajian pustaka yang meneliti terkait dengan pengimplementasian AI terhadap customer experience. Baik yang hanya terfokus pada personalisasi pelanggan hingga yang menerapkan lebih dari satu jenis AI dalam satu platform e-commerce yang sama. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui pengaruh berbagai jenis implementasi AI yang diterapkan pada platform e-commerce di Indonesia. Platform e-commerce yang dipilih sebagai fokus dalam penelitian ini adalah Shopee, Tokopedia, Lazada, Tiktok Shop, dan Blibli. Berdasarkan hasil penelitian, didapatkan bahwa implementasi AI secara keseluruhan mampu menjadi strategi penting dalam persaingan pasar yang semakin kompetitif untuk jenis e-commerce sejenis yang ada di Indonesia. Pengimplementasian AI memiliki pengaruh terhadap customer experience pada e-commerce yang digunakan di Indonesia, baik secara langsung maupun secara tidak langsung. Hal ini secara garis besar memberikan dampak positif sekaligus dampak negatif, bergantung pada variabel yang menyertai saat melakukan penelitian. Perlu ada pula pertimbangan risiko kebocoran data dan risiko invasif ketika mengimplementasikan AI di platform apa pun, termasuk platform e-commerce. Implementasi AI di e-commerce mampu memberikan solusi atas masalah di masa lalu, tetapi perlu diawasi keamanan data yang tersimpan di dalam platform tersebut agar customer experience semakin meningkat.

title: Title: Dynamic Topology-Based Error Correction for Quantum Circuits
abstract: Quantum computing promises revolutionary advancements in computation and information processing, but its inherent fragility makes error correction a critical hurdle. Current error correction techniques often rely on static topology, limiting the system's ability to adapt to evolving errors. This paper introduces a novel dynamic topology-based error correction method, leveraging a real-time feedback loop to dynamically adjust the circuit topology to mitigate errors. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and preliminary experiments, achieving significantly improved fidelity compared to traditional methods. This work provides a fundamental step toward enabling more robust and reliable quantum computations.

title: Title: Non-linear Quantum-Classical Coherence for Sensor Networks
abstract: Quantum-classical coherence is a promising paradigm for enhancing sensor network robustness and data transmission rates. Classical networks suffer from noise and bandwidth limitations, hindering their performance. This paper explores a novel quantum-classical coherence scheme designed to mitigate these challenges by integrating quantum sensors and classical processing. We propose a method to enhance data quality through quantum-enhanced coherence, offering a potential breakthrough in sensor network design. The core claim is that this approach significantly improves data reliability and transmission rates compared to traditional sensor networks. We detail the proposed scheme, outlining the key components and the mathematical framework underlying the enhanced coherence. The paper will discuss the implications of this work for various sensor network applications.

title: Based on Simulated Evolution Algorithm for System Design (BEASD)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to complex system design, termed Based on Simulated Evolution Algorithm for System Design (BEASD). The core idea is to frame system design as an evolutionary problem, leveraging the power of Simulated Evolution Algorithms (SEA) to iteratively refine system structure and parameters. BEASD employs a population-based search strategy, mimicking the biological evolution process of selection, crossover, and mutation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method in tackling complex design challenges, offering a potentially more robust and adaptable solution compared to traditional design methods. The paper outlines the theoretical framework, detailing the algorithm's components and operational principles. It then presents a conceptual application demonstrating the core functionality of BEASD, illustrating how it can be applied to optimize system parameters within a defined objective function. Further research directions are suggested, focusing on the scalability and applicability of BEASD to diverse system domains.

title: 基于自适应的量子机器学习的概率模型优化
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) offers the potential for significant advancements in computational capabilities, particularly in areas requiring complex data analysis and pattern recognition. However, the inherent complexity of quantum algorithms often necessitates careful parameter optimization, a process traditionally reliant on human intervention. This paper presents a novel approach to quantum machine learning – a probabilistic model optimization algorithm based on adaptive parameter adjustment – designed to dramatically improve training efficiency and model performance. We introduce a method that dynamically adjusts the parameters of a probabilistic model, leveraging self-tuning capabilities to achieve a more robust and efficient training cycle. This represents a significant step forward, addressing a critical bottleneck in the development of quantum machine learning models.

title: Title: Adaptive Geometry of Quantum Entanglement
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, possesses a remarkable property: its ability to correlate states across vast distances without physical transmission. However, harnessing this entanglement for practical applications, particularly in quantum information processing, faces significant challenges. This paper explores a novel approach to quantum entanglement – Adaptive Geometry of Quantum Entanglement – that leverages the inherent dynamism of quantum systems to achieve more complex and efficient information storage and manipulation. We propose a framework based on dynamically adjusting the topology of quantum systems, driven by a concept of "dynamic topology fields." This approach aims to overcome limitations of traditional entanglement-based techniques by offering a fundamentally different pathway to information processing. The core claim is that by constructing multi-scale quantum topological structures, we can achieve more complex and enhanced information storage and processing capabilities. title: STREAM-BSG: A Streaming Graph Architecture for Real-Time Fraud Detection in B2B Payment Networks
abstract: STREAM-BSG maintains an incremental buyer-supplier graph in a streaming state store and computes a 49-dimensional feature vector online - 15 node, 18 edge, 14 subgraph, and 2 current-row change-detection features - before classification with XGBoost. It targets business-to-business payment fraud rather than the business-to-consumer card fraud most academic work addresses, and formalizes five fraud topologies documented in industry practice: vendor injection, invoice cycling, payment-term manipulation, shell-supplier rings, and wire redirection. This repository holds the companion code, figures, datasets, and full reproduction pipeline for the paper.

title: Contextual Graph Neural Networks with Memory Resonance
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) termed Contextual Graph Neural Networks with Memory Resonance (CGNMR). The core idea is that GNNs can significantly benefit from incorporating a mechanism that allows nodes to 'remember' and react to previously observed patterns, effectively propagating contextual information across the graph. The proposed CGNMR architecture integrates a recurrent connection within the GNN, creating a dynamic, context-aware representation. This allows nodes to not only process information from their immediate neighbors but also to leverage historical information, leading to improved performance in tasks such as node classification, link prediction, and graph classification. The key contribution lies in the synergistic combination of graph convolutional operations with recurrent memory networks, resulting in a more holistic understanding of graph structures and enhanced predictive capabilities. Mathematical formulations and notation are presented to explicitly define the model and its components.

title: Dynamic Probability Field Theory for Quantum Entanglement Analysis
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic probability field theory designed to analyze quantum entanglement properties and predict its evolution. We propose a framework that treats entanglement as a dynamically evolving probability field, incorporating self-adaptive properties to enhance quantum computation's efficiency and reliability. The core mechanism involves representing entanglement as a continuously evolving probability field, allowing for a more nuanced understanding and control over its behavior. The paper details the theoretical foundation and initial experimental explorations of this approach, highlighting its potential for improved entanglement analysis and quantum algorithm design. The primary goal is to provide a robust mathematical model for understanding and predicting entanglement dynamics.

title: Probabilistic Logic Reasoning Engine for Enhanced Decision-Making
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to decision-making systems by constructing a Probabilistic Logic Reasoning Engine (PLRE). The core of the engine lies in the synergistic combination of probabilistic graph models and logical inference algorithms. This integration enables the engine to effectively handle uncertainty and ambiguity inherent in real-world data, ultimately leading to more robust and reliable decision outcomes. The engine leverages probability inference within probabilistic graph models to capture relationships between variables and then applies logical constraints to refine the inferences based on predefined rules and knowledge. This approach addresses the limitations of traditional systems that rely solely on either probabilistic or logical reasoning, providing a more comprehensive solution for complex decision scenarios. The engine's architecture is designed for modularity and extensibility, allowing for the incorporation of diverse data sources and knowledge representations. The effectiveness of the PLRE is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, outlining a framework for future development and implementation. ---

title: Adaptive Neuron Connection for Quantum Neural Networks
abstract: Quantum neural networks (QNNs) hold immense promise for revolutionizing artificial intelligence, offering the potential for enhanced learning and complex pattern recognition. However, training QNNs often requires significant computational resources and time, hindering their widespread adoption. This paper introduces an innovative approach to QNNs – the Adaptive Neuron Connection (ANC) – designed to address this challenge by implementing a dynamic adjustment mechanism for neural neuron connections. This system leverages the inherent adaptability of quantum systems to dynamically adjust connection weights based on input signal variations, thereby reducing computational burden and improving model performance. We detail the architecture of the ANC, its operational principles, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness in several benchmark datasets. The core of this design lies in a novel dynamic weight adjustment algorithm that ensures optimal network performance across a wide range of input conditions. This work provides a new framework for QNNs, offering a pathway towards more efficient and scalable learning.

title: Dynamic Topological Language Quantum Modeling
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum modeling, termed Dynamic Topological Language Quantum Modeling, that leverages the inherent properties of quantum computation to automatically adjust the structure of a dynamic topological language and achieve precise modeling and prediction of topological structure patterns. The method employs a quantum-enhanced iterative process that adapts to input data, providing a significant advancement over traditional methods. The core mechanism centers around utilizing quantum algorithms to dynamically restructure the topological language, while simultaneously employing quantum-enhanced dimensionality reduction techniques to facilitate precise prediction. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary simulations, highlighting its potential for significant improvements in the modeling and prediction of complex topological phenomena.

title: Adaptive Bayesian Networks for Real-Time Anomaly Detection
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to real-time anomaly detection utilizing adaptive Bayesian Networks (ABNs). Traditional Bayesian Networks (BNs) often struggle with dynamic systems due to their static nature, leading to inaccurate detection and elevated false positive rates. This research addresses this limitation by incorporating a reinforcement learning (RL)-based adaptation strategy within the BN structure and parameters. The system learns from incoming data streams, identifying and adapting to evolving system dynamics and changing data distributions. The core idea is to construct a BN that modifies its structure and associated probabilities based on observed anomalies, effectively creating a self-learning anomaly detection system. The proposed ABN framework utilizes a Markov Decision Process (MDP) formulation, where the BN acts as the agent, interacting with the environment (the data stream) to minimize the cumulative reward of false positives and false negatives. The system's adaptability is evaluated through simulations, demonstrating its superior performance compared to static BNs in dynamic environments. The key contribution is the integration of Bayesian Networks with adaptive reinforcement learning, providing a robust and scalable solution for real-time anomaly detection.

abstract: This paper presents a novel optimization algorithm based on multi-dimensional non-linear function spaces, specifically designed for enhancing machine learning model training. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with complex non-linear relationships, and this approach addresses this limitation by incorporating non-linear function constraints into the optimization process. The core mechanism involves introducing non-linear function spaces, leveraging optimization algorithms to navigate these spaces and find optimal parameter values, ultimately leading to improved model performance. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this algorithm in training machine learning models, showcasing its potential for accelerating model development and achieving higher accuracy.

title: Rewards, Regrets, and Rubber Arms: A Comparative Analysis Review of Reinforcement Learning in Games and Robotics
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Reinforcement Learning in Games and Robotics in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of reinforcement learning and robotics as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Klasifikasi Sentimen Ulasan Pengguna Aplikasi Alfagift Menggunakan Metode Support Vector Machine Berbasis TF-IDF
abstract: The rapid development of digital technology has driven the increasing use of mobile applications in the retail sector, one of which is the Alfagift application developed by PT Sumber Alfaria Trijaya Tbk. User reviews on Google Play Store contain valuable information regarding user satisfaction and complaints, yet their large volume makes manual analysis inefficient, necessitating an automated approach. This study aims to classify the sentiment of Alfagift user reviews into three classes: Positive, Negative, and Neutral, using the Support Vector Machine (SVM) method with Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) feature representation. A total of 4,937 reviews were collected through web scraping and processed through preprocessing stages including case folding, slang normalization, tokenization, stopword removal, and stemming. Feature extraction used TF-IDF with unigram-bigram configuration and a maximum of 10,000 features, with an 80:20 data split ratio. The model was evaluated using a confusion matrix and 10-fold Stratified Cross Validation. The results show a test accuracy of 87.15% and a cross-validation average of 87.28% (standard deviation 1.0368%). The Positive and Negative classes were classified well (F1-score 0.9172 and 0.8676), while the Neutral class was poorly classified due to extreme class imbalance, representing only 4.7% of the entire dataset.

title: Seeing the City or Recognizing the Place? What Street-View Imagery Adds Beyond Existing Urban Data in VLM-Based Urban Sensing
abstract: Street-view imagery is increasingly analysed with vision-language models (VLMs) to infer urban attributes, but predictive accuracy alone does not show how much a photograph contributes beyond data already available for the same place. Using three VLMs, we compare image-based predictions with existing urban data for seven attributes drawn from five public resources. Each urban unit is evaluated with imagery, with location or text context, and against non-image predictions from nearby observations or public records. We also replace images and add conflicting records to test which source the predictions follow. Nearby observations or public records matched or exceeded image-only predictions for road damage, curb ramps, population, and house price. Images were more informative for building type, building function, and the floor count of low-rise buildings. For floor count, the advantage of images over nearby OpenStreetMap labels increased by 5.7 percentage points per doubling of distance to the nearest labelled building and declined for tall buildings whose rooflines often fell outside the frame. When images and records disagreed, predictions usually moved towards the supplied record. Released OpenFACADES floor annotations, generated with OpenStreetMap floor values as input, showed the same dependence: their agreement with the reference increased with building height, whereas that of image-only reruns decreased. The value of street-view imagery therefore depends on whether an attribute is visible and how well the place is already covered by existing data. Because machine-derived labels are often reused as references, these comparisons also bear on how urban datasets are documented and evaluated.

title: GDB-Reward: From Evaluation Metrics to Training Rewards for Graphic Design
abstract: Text-to-image models excel at natural image synthesis but struggle with graphic design, where success depends on satisfying precise constraints on typography, layout, color, and visual communication. While prompt optimization offers an attractive alternative to expensive diffusion model fine-tuning, learning prompts for frozen image generators requires informative reward functions despite the entirely non-differentiable generation process. Reinforcement learning does not require differentiable objectives; it requires only scalar rewards capable of ranking candidate outputs. This raises a simple question: can design evaluation metrics themselves become reinforcement learning rewards? Our central contribution is GDB-Reward, a framework that systematically transforms heterogeneous graphic design evaluation metrics into a unified reinforcement learning reward. Experiments demonstrate that GDB-Reward provides an effective optimization objective, substantially improving adherence to the design specification in perceptual quality, rendering fidelity, and spatial accuracy while keeping the image generator entirely frozen. More broadly, our results demonstrate that heterogeneous, non-differentiable evaluation metrics can move beyond passive benchmarking to become effective optimization objectives for reinforcement learning in domains where differentiable supervision is unavailable.

title: CrashDiffuser: VLM-Guided Collision Intent Reasoning for Fine-Grained Safety-Critical Traffic Scenario Generation
abstract: Generating safety-critical scenarios is essential for evaluating autonomous driving systems. However, existing generators primarily focus on inducing collisions and offer limited control over where contact occurs on the target vehicle. In this paper, we study fine-grained safety-critical scenario generation, where success requires both a target collision and a specified head, rear, or side contact region. We propose CrashDiffuser, a closed-loop VLM-guided diffusion framework that decouples semantic collision reasoning from continuous trajectory synthesis through a hierarchical collision-intent interface derived from the requested target contact region. At initialization, the VLM extracts reusable scene-level context; at each replanning step, it predicts a structured action tuple describing speed change, turning behavior, and collision stage. This intent conditions a diffusion model to generate executable adversarial trajectories, while collision-guided sampling, candidate selection, and short-horizon replanning adapt generation to the target vehicle's evolving behavior. On WOMD-derived closed-loop scenarios, CrashDiffuser achieves a target-collision rate of 50.33% in a single attempt and 67.98% after three attempts, together with a contact-region control success rate of 40.05% and competitive trajectory naturalness. Component ablations further support the proposed design.

title: C$^2$T-OpenMax: A Novel Open-Set WiFi RF Fingerprinting Method via Center Constrained Learning and Confidence-Guided Tail Modeling
abstract: Radio frequency fingerprinting (RFF) enables device authentication from transmitter-specific hardware imperfections, but practical deployment requires cross-environment open-set recognition. Data augmentation improves environmental generalization, yet may yield dispersed, low-confidence known-class representations that distort the class statistics used by OpenMax. To address this problem, we propose C$^2$T-OpenMax, an enhanced OpenMax framework combining center-constrained learning with confidence-guided tail modeling. The former improves intra-class compactness, making class-wise representations more suitable for distance-based modeling. The latter retains only correctly classified, high-confidence logits for mean activation vector estimation and Weibull fitting, reducing bias from ambiguous boundary samples. Together, the two modules refine representation geometry and OpenMax construction while preserving augmentation benefits. Experiments on a public WiFi CSI dataset show that C$^2$T-OpenMax achieves the highest open-set accuracy in seven of eight location groups and outperforms all baselines in area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and open-set classification rate (OSCR) across every tested openness level. Under the largest-openness setting, it improves accuracy by 12.31%, AUROC by 0.0887, and OSCR by 0.0856 over the augmented OpenMax baseline.

title: Morphological Hijacking in Frozen Language Models: A Contrastive, Symmetry-Regularized Projection Head for Algebraic Structure Recovery
abstract: Preprint, v3. Not yet peer-reviewed. Frozen autoregressive language models cluster surface-similar tokenstogether even when a stronger, task-relevant structure is available inthe input. This paper documents "morphological hijacking" — near-totalcollapse of algebraic-structure recovery under adversarial surfacecorrelation — across four frozen model families (GPT2-small, Pythia-410m,Mistral-7B-v0.3, Qwen2.5-7B), traces it to representational anisotropy,and introduces a lightweight, trainable projection head (contrastiveobjective + positional-symmetry penalty + rogue-dimension ablation +Soft-PCA initialization) that substantially recovers the structure. Theresult is validated at both the discrete-clustering level (Adjusted RandIndex) and the continuous embedding-geometry level (margin, win rate)across five architecturally diverse models, and further tested onnatural English words, a freshly generated 10x-larger constructedlexicon, and (v2) a dedicated test of true algebraic group-positionrecovery with a shuffled-label control. New in v3: a full pre-registered diagnostic pilot testing whether thesame remediation strategy recovers true algebraic COMPOSITION (not justcategory/position classification) — i.e., whether z_i + z_j can berecovered from two independent operand representations. This pilotdocuments a complete, honestly-reported negative result: after rulingout optimization failure, numerical ill-conditioning, and geometricmisalignment between operand representations in turn, and afterconfirming a capacity-controlled MLP fits seen pairs almost perfectly,the same MLP fails to generalize to unseen ordered pairs, falling belowboth a shuffled-label and a wrong-operation control — a cleanmemorization signature, not evidence of learned composition. This resultprecisely delineates what the paper's remediation strategy does and doesnot demonstrate about frozen language models' algebraic structure. Several negative results are reported throughout, including a rejected"globally architectural anisotropy" hypothesis and a rejectedlayer-selection heuristic. This is a preliminary, honestly-scopedempirical report, not a claim of general applicability. Limitations, afull pre-submission checklist, and complete reproducibility code(including the composition-pilot diagnostic chain) are included. title: Title: Algorithmic Quantum Simulation of Biological Metastasis via Spatio-Temporal Topology
abstract: This paper explores the potential of algorithmic quantum simulation to model the evolution of biological metastasis through the intricate interplay of spatial topology. Traditional simulations struggle to adequately capture the complex, dynamic nature of this phenomenon, particularly the subtle shifts in network structure that drive the process. We propose a novel quantum map approach to represent biological systems, leveraging quantum entanglement and superposition to simulate the propagation of microorganisms. The core mechanism focuses on modeling the progression of spatial topology – the arrangement of nodes and connections – as it evolves across time, providing a fundamentally new framework for understanding metastasis. This research investigates the feasibility of simulating key stages of metastasis, including initial contact, clonal expansion, and the formation of metastatic colonies, utilizing quantum-enhanced computational tools. The proposed method promises a significant advancement in our comprehension of biological systems, offering a pathway to more accurate and insightful simulations of complex biological processes.

title: 基于自适应的概率场论的量子算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum algorithm based on an adaptive probability field theory (APFT) that automatically adjusts quantum particle parameters to optimize quantum computation performance and enhance the efficiency of quantum algorithms. Traditional quantum algorithms often require manual parameter tuning, which is a time-consuming and error-prone process. Our proposed algorithm leverages adaptive parameter adjustment driven by quantum algorithm optimization to achieve significant performance improvements and stability in quantum computations. The core mechanism involves a dynamic adjustment of the quantum state, guided by a feedback loop that continuously evaluates the algorithm's progress and adjusts parameters to maintain optimal performance. This approach offers a substantial improvement over existing methods, potentially unlocking new capabilities in quantum computation.

title: The title: Topological Topology and the Association of Natural Language Information
abstract: This paper investigates the intriguing intersection of topology and natural language information, proposing a novel approach to enhance the accuracy of natural language understanding. The inherent structure of topological spaces provides a powerful framework for representing and analyzing language's complexities. We explore the potential of leveraging topological structures as a latent feature within natural language data, aiming to create a robust and adaptable model for semantic interpretation. The core of this work lies in the development of a model that dynamically infers the underlying topological properties of language, enabling a deeper and more nuanced understanding of meaning. This research contributes to a paradigm shift in natural language processing, moving beyond traditional statistical methods towards a more holistic and geometrically-informed approach to language representation. Specifically, we construct a model that maps linguistic expressions to topological spaces, enabling the identification of underlying relationships and patterns within the language's structure. The resulting model exhibits improved performance in tasks requiring semantic reasoning and contextual interpretation, demonstrating the significant potential of integrating topological analysis into the field of natural language understanding. This work represents a crucial step towards creating more intelligent and contextually aware language processing systems.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning algorithm, termed Quantum Adaptive Topology-Based Learning (QATL), leveraging the principles of quantum self-adapted topology to enhance learning capabilities. We demonstrate the effectiveness of QATL through the successful application to a range of complex pattern recognition tasks. The algorithm's core mechanism involves dynamically adjusting a topological structure to capture intricate relationships within the data, leading to improved predictive accuracy and decision-making. The study explores the potential of this approach to overcome limitations of traditional machine learning techniques, particularly in situations involving high dimensionality and complex non-linear correlations. We analyze the algorithm's strengths and weaknesses, highlighting key design choices and potential avenues for future research. The paper concludes with a discussion of the implications of this approach for various applications, including anomaly detection and data compression.

title: Dynamic Program Abstraction Semantic Consistency Verification (DPSCV)
abstract: This paper introduces Dynamic Program Abstraction Semantic Consistency Verification (DPSCV), a novel approach to ensuring the correctness of dynamic program abstraction. Dynamic program abstraction is a powerful technique for simplifying complex programs, but its success hinges on maintaining semantic consistency across abstraction levels. Traditional static analysis techniques often fail to capture the dynamic nature of abstraction, leading to potential semantic errors. DPSCV addresses this limitation by formally verifying the consistency of abstraction hierarchies using a model checking framework. The core idea is to represent each abstraction level as a state in a state space, enabling systematic verification of the relationships between levels. This paper details the methodology, outlining the key components of the DPSCV framework and illustrating its application with a concrete example. The central claim of DPSCV is that rigorous verification of semantic consistency is paramount for the reliable application of dynamic program abstraction. The core mechanism is a model-checking based approach, providing a systematic method for ensuring the accuracy of the abstraction process.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Topological Field Theory
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic self-adaptive topological field theory, leveraging quantum entanglement to enable instantaneous adjustment of computational topology and achieve unprecedented levels of parallel computation. We propose a new concept, the "Quantum Entanglement Topological" (QET) framework, which utilizes quantum entanglement to dynamically modify the topology of a field, optimizing it in real-time. This approach overcomes limitations of existing topological field theories, offering a fundamentally new computational paradigm. We demonstrate the theoretical foundations and preliminary experimental results supporting this approach, highlighting its potential for transformative advancements in parallel computing.

title: Developing a Transparent Verification Mechanism for Digital Certificates Issued by OpenXPKI using a Merkle Tree
abstract: Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) has traditionally relied on centralized Certificate Authorities (CAs), and this architecture introduces a critical single point of failure; a compromised CA can issue fraudulent certificates without immediate detection. In this context, traditional validation protocols, such as CRLs and OCSP, operate reactively post-issuance and fail to architecturally prevent unauthorized generation. This research addresses this architectural gap by designing and implementing a Certificate Transparency (CT) mechanism that is managed locally within an OpenXPKI enterprise environment. This architecture enables independent cryptographic verification of certificate issuance operations while keeping sensitive internal network data isolated from public registries. The proposed system strictly enforces pre-issuance logging by modifying the OpenXPKI workflow to generate a preliminary certificate prior to the final issuance of an X.509 certificate. This preliminary certificate is registered on a standalone server (CT Log) based on a Merkle Tree structure. Following registration, the server issues a Signed Certificate Timestamp (SCT) that is directly embedded in the final certificate structure, while a client-side web application employs a tile-based storage model to support independent cryptographic verification. Experimental evaluations have demonstrated the system's ability to deterministically detect any retroactive tampering with records. The fail-closed architecture also succeeded in categorically preventing the issuance of any unverified certificates during server failure simulations. On the operational level, performance measurements confirmed that this integration adds a delay of less than one second to the issuance cycle, with a linear growth in hash tile storage of 32 bytes per added certificate. These results confirm that incorporating a Merkle Tree-based verification layer into enterprise infrastructure replaces trust assumptions with mathematical proofs, providing organizations with tamper-evident auditing capabilities without compromising operational efficiency.

title: Title: Multi-Scale Information Fusion of a Non-Linear Model
abstract: This paper introduces a novel multi-scale information fusion model designed to enhance prediction accuracy by integrating information from diverse scales. The core aim is to address the inherent challenges of complex data by employing a non-linear model that facilitates a deeper understanding and integration of these varying levels of detail. We propose a framework that dynamically adjusts the weighting of different scale features based on the specific context of the data, leading to improved model performance across a range of applications. The model's architecture is built upon a combination of feature extraction, hierarchical modeling, and non-linear transformations to capture the intricate relationships within the data. The paper details the model's design, training procedure, and validation results, demonstrating its effectiveness in predicting complex patterns. This work represents a significant advancement in multi-scale data integration, offering a robust and adaptable solution for various analytical tasks.

title: Graph Wavelets for Time Series Anomaly Detection
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to time series anomaly detection utilizing graph wavelets. Traditional methods frequently struggle to effectively identify anomalies within time series data characterized by intricate temporal dependencies. Our method leverages graph wavelets to transform time series data into a graph representation, where data points are nodes and temporal relationships are represented by edges. This graph structure is then analyzed using wavelet transforms, allowing for the detection of anomalies based on deviations from the expected graph structure. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this technique through a theoretical framework and explore its potential applications. The core claim is that traditional methods fail to capture complex temporal patterns, and this work proposes a solution using graph wavelets. This approach offers a more robust and accurate method for anomaly detection in time series data with complex relationships.

title: Multi-Modal Implicit Knowledge Graph Construction
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to constructing knowledge graphs from implicit, multi-modal data. Traditional knowledge graph construction heavily relies on manual annotation, a process that is both time-consuming and expensive. Our method leverages the rich information contained within user behavior data – encompassing text, images, and videos – to automatically infer hidden knowledge and relationships. We employ deep learning models to represent these diverse modalities within a shared embedding space. Subsequently, we utilize similarity measures or graph neural networks to identify correlations and construct the knowledge graph. This approach significantly reduces the reliance on labeled data and offers a scalable solution for knowledge graph creation, particularly in scenarios where explicit knowledge bases are unavailable or incomplete. The core claim is that analyzing multi-modal user behavior data can effectively build a knowledge graph representing implicit knowledge and relationships. The key mechanism involves mapping different data modalities into a shared vector space using deep learning, followed by relationship discovery through similarity or graph neural networks. This work contributes to a more efficient and automated approach to knowledge graph construction, paving the way for intelligent applications that can reason and understand complex information.

title: Graph Neural Network Based Social Network Structure Prediction
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for predicting the structure and evolution of social networks. Traditional methods for social network analysis often rely on static network features and struggle to capture the dynamic nature of these complex systems. We propose a novel framework utilizing GNNs to learn the intricate patterns and relationships within social networks, enabling us to forecast future network configurations. The core mechanism involves constructing a GNN model that effectively integrates node and edge information to represent social network dynamics. The model then employs predictive algorithms to estimate the future state of the network. This approach represents a significant advancement in social network prediction, offering a more sophisticated and adaptable methodology compared to existing techniques. The research demonstrates the potential of GNNs to model and anticipate changes within social networks, with implications for various fields including social science, marketing, and public health.

title: Based on Biological Neural Networks for Explainable AI
abstract: This paper investigates the application of biologically inspired neural networks (BiNNs) to the field of Explainable AI (XAI). The core argument presented is that the inherent structure and function of BiNNs offer a natural pathway to constructing AI systems with intrinsic explainability. Traditional artificial neural networks (ANNs) often operate as "black boxes," making it difficult to understand the reasoning behind their decisions. In contrast, BiNNs, modeled after biological neural networks, possess features such as localized connections, adaptive dynamics, and inherent self-organization that lend themselves to greater transparency. This work proposes a framework for building XAI systems leveraging these characteristics. Specifically, we aim to simulate the synaptic connections and neuronal activity of biological networks to generate neural network models with explicitly interpretable components. Furthermore, we explore the utilization of BiNNs' self-organizing capabilities to enhance the transparency of the model's decision-making process. The presented approach addresses the growing need for AI systems that can not only produce accurate predictions but also provide understandable explanations for their outputs, fostering trust and accountability. The research focuses on the theoretical foundations and potential mechanisms of this novel approach, laying the groundwork for future development and experimentation.

title: Towards Automated Accessibility Adaptation of Learning Materials with Compact Large Language Models
abstract: This paper investigates the use of locally deployed Compact Large Language Models (CLLMs) to support inclusive education by automatically adapting learning materials for students with diverse accessibility needs. We propose a structured framework for multi-profile accessibility adaptation based on explicit, constraint-driven transformations, modeling learner profiles (e.g., dyslexia, ADHD, visual impairments) as sets of formalized requirements integrated into a modular pipeline. To support practical use, we also developed a web-based interface that allows users to input educational content, select a learner profile and a language model, and generate adapted versions of the text. We evaluate the framework using three locally executed models: Llama 3 8B, Mistral 7B, and Phi-3 Mini. Results show that larger models better comply with complex constraints, though all models exhibit limitations, including partial adherence to constraints and formatting issues. These findings highlight both the potential and the current limitations of LLM-based approaches for scalable accessibility support in education.

evidence.title: Towards Automated Accessibility Adaptation of Learning Materials with Compact Large Language Models
evidence.abstract: This paper investigates the use of locally deployed Compact Large Language Models (CLLMs) to support inclusive education by automatically adapting learning materials for students with diverse accessibility needs. We propose a structured framework for multi-profile accessibility adaptation based on explicit, constraint-driven transformations, modeling learner profiles (e.g., dyslexia, ADHD, visual impairments) as sets of formalized requirements integrated into a modular pipeline. To support practical use, we also developed a web-based interface that allows users to input educational content, select a learner profile and a language model, and generate adapted versions of the text. We evaluate the framework using three locally executed models: Llama 3 8B, Mistral 7B, and Phi-3 Mini. Results show that larger models better comply with complex constraints, though all models exhibit limitations, including partial adherence to constraints and formatting issues. These findings highlight both the potential and the current limitations of LLM-based approaches for scalable accessibility support in education.

title: Design a neuro-heuristic Morlet wavelet neural network procedure for the reactive transport system
abstract: This work shows the numerical performance through stochastic paradigms of the Reactive Transport System (RTS). The design of the solver is presented through the Morlet wavelet function, which works as an artificial neural network and the hybridization of a genetic algorithm and an active set. An objective function is created using the differential RTS, which is optimized through the hybrid capability of the designed scheme. The precision of the solver is perceived in comparison with the obtained and reference outcomes, the absolute error, and the number of multiple executions based on different operators. The inspiration to exploit the Morlet wavelet neural network process and the hybridization methods is to present precise and reliable solutions for solving the nonlinear and stiff differential systems. Three RTS cases are numerically treated to validate the efficiency of the designed process, and the performance of the scheme is also validated by using different statistical operators.

title: Large Language Models (LLMs) for Telecom Root Cause Analysis (RCA): A Structured Reasoning Framework for Evidence-Grounded Diagnosis
abstract: Root cause analysis (RCA) is a critical task in telecom network operations, but diagnosing performance degradations in modern 5G and emerging 6G networks remains challenging due to complex cross-layer dependencies. While large language models (LLMs) offer promising capabilities for reasoning and knowledge integration, directly applying vanilla LLMs to telecom RCA often leads to hallucination, unstable reasoning, and poor alignment with structured network evidence. This work first reviews the evolution of telecom RCA from rule-based and machine learning (ML) approaches to emerging LLM-enabled techniques, and provides an overview of recent paradigms, including structured reasoning, retrieval-augmented knowledge grounding, agentic orchestration, and verifiable reasoning. Building upon these insights, we propose a structured reasoning framework for LLM-enabled telecom RCA that aligns diagnostic reasoning with telecom-specific evidence and domain knowledge. The proposed approach first organizes heterogeneous network telemetry into canonical contexts, and then enforces decision-path reasoning during diagnosis, and finally generates evidence-grounded explanations for reliable fault identification. Experimental results on two 5G RCA datasets, TeleLogs and TelecomTS, demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently improves diagnostic accuracy and decision consistency compared with baseline techniques. These cross-dataset results highlight the importance of structured reasoning design for practical LLM-based RCA systems in next-generation telecom networks.

title: Beauty is in the AI of the beholder: MLLMs systematically overrate facial attractiveness
abstract: Beauty assessments from Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are increasingly popular amongst users, companies, and aestheticians. This raises the question of whether these AI models can accurately reflect human judgments of attractiveness. In a pre- registered exploratory study, we compared the attractiveness ratings of 2,513 human participants to four widely used commercial AI models: Claude, Gemini, GPT, and Grok. Results showed that MLLMs systematically rate faces more favourably and within a narrower range than humans and, at the time of study, do not reproduce human ratings in absolute terms. However, MLLMs exhibit strong correlations with human attractiveness judgments, accurately tracking the rank-ordering of faces. MLLMs may judge faces by different cues than humans; only face age was a predictor of facial attractiveness in both humans and MLLMs, with inconsistent patterns across models for ethnicity and gender. AI models strongly agree with one another, except for Grok, which also showed the lowest agreement with humans. Our findings suggest that while they may be able to approximate rank-orderings of human attractiveness, current off-the-shelf commercial MLLMs systematically overrate the beauty of human faces.

title: Retrosynthesis of Synthetic Media for Explainable AI Provenance Forensics
abstract: With the rapid proliferation of generative models on Machine Learning as a Service (MLaaS) platforms, reliably tracing the provenance of synthetic media without modifying generator architectures or parameters remains a major challenge. In this work, we propose a self-referential retrosynthesis framework for explainable AI provenance forensics under a fixed-generator setting. The framework leverages a jointly optimized encoder-decoder pair to implement a self-embedding mechanism that enables round-trip consistency verification. During inference, client inputs are first encoded and then processed by the generator to produce outputs with high visual fidelity. For forensic verification, the consistency between the resynthesized image and the query image is analyzed to determine whether the image originates from the target generative model. Our approach eliminates the need for watermark embedding or modifications to the generation process. Experimental results show that images generated from encoded inputs maintain visual quality comparable to original generator outputs, while decoded images reliably trace back to their corresponding source inputs. Furthermore, the framework provides interpretable evidence for generative content provenance, establishing a practical tool for explainable generative AI forensics.

title: LaST-SR: Laplace-Inspired Steady-Transient Complex-Frequency Decomposition for Single Image Super-Resolution
abstract: Single-image super-resolution (SISR) requires global context modeling for structurally consistent reconstruction. Fourier operators are increasingly adopted for global feature modeling. However, their periodic spectral bases constrain the representation of localized aperiodic variations, limiting the recovery of irregular structures and fine details. In dynamical systems, the Laplace neural operator extends Fourier modes to complex frequencies and decomposes the output signal into complementary steady-state and transient responses to jointly model periodic and aperiodic information. We derive, for the first time, an approximate steady-transient decomposition for two-dimensional feature maps, providing an analytical basis for the proposed complex-frequency decomposition. Accordingly, we propose LaST-SR, centered on a Complex-Frequency Decomposition module that couples a global full-spectrum Fourier branch for image-wide dependencies and long-range structural consistency with a window-conditioned local complex-frequency branch for localized, content-dependent aperiodic variations. To fuse the resulting features, we further design a Steady-Transient Collaborative Aggregation module for cross-branch interaction and joint aggregation. Experiments on five benchmarks show that LaST-SR achieves the best PSNR/SSIM among the compared methods for $\times2$ and $\times4$ SISR. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of the proposed architecture and its key modeling mechanisms.

title: MCP Servers in Agentic AI - Architecture, Adoption, and Security of the Model Context Protocol
abstract: The Model Context Protocol (MCP), introduced by Anthropic in late 2024, has emerged as a widely adopted open standard forconnecting large language model (LLM) applications to external tools, data sources, and services. By standardizing the interfacebetween an AI host application and the servers that expose capabilities to it, MCP has been described as a USB-C-like connectorfor agentic AI, replacing bespoke, one-off integrations with a single, reusable protocol. This paper explains how MCP servers work within agentic AI systems: the host-client-server architecture, the JSON-RPC 2.0 messaging layer, the core primitives of tools, resources, and prompts, and the rapid evolution of the specification from an initial local-only design to a stateless, horizontally scalable protocol core in its 2026-07-28 revision. We review the growing ecosystem of MCP servers and the parallel emergence of complementary agent-to-agent protocols, synthesize empirical security research documenting tool poisoning, indirect prompt injection, and auto-execution vulnerabilities across production AI coding tools, and summarize benchmarking efforts that evaluate LLM agents against real-world MCP server environments. We conclude with governance guidance for deploying MCP servers safely in production agentic systems and an agenda for future research.

title: Non-linear Topological Geometry Adaptive Constraint Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of adaptive constraint optimization techniques to complex systems, specifically focusing on non-linear topological geometry. The core idea centers around leveraging the inherent dynamism of topological structures to dynamically adjust constraints, enabling the identification of optimal solutions within complex, evolving systems. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with these structures, necessitating a novel approach that utilizes topological information to facilitate robust and adaptable solutions. We propose a new algorithm that integrates a "topological information" objective, dynamically adjusts constraint parameters based on the structure's evolution, and ultimately aims to find optimal solutions in complex systems. This research presents a framework for efficient and adaptive optimization, particularly relevant for systems requiring dynamic adjustment of constraints.

title: Dynamic Topology Spaces and Topology Migration Algorithms
abstract: Dynamic Topology Spaces (DTS) offers a novel approach to machine learning by leveraging the inherent adaptability of topological spaces. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, Dynamic Topology Migration (DTM), designed to automatically transfer the structural characteristics of a source topology to a target topology. We propose a neural network architecture that learns a dynamic representation of the source topology and then iteratively migrates this representation to the target topology, enabling flexible and adaptable machine learning across diverse tasks and scenarios. This work addresses the limitations of static topology transfer methods by introducing a dynamic learning mechanism that allows the algorithm to continuously refine its representation and optimize performance. The proposed DTM demonstrates significant improvements in task performance and robustness compared to existing approaches, particularly in scenarios requiring significant structural change.

title: Dynamic Topology Search Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic topology search algorithm designed to enhance search efficiency. Traditional search algorithms often rely on manual design, limiting their adaptability. Our algorithm leverages the inherent properties of dynamic topology to dynamically adjust search strategies, resulting in improved performance. We present a theoretical framework and initial implementation demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach, focusing on optimizing the exploration of complex search spaces. The core mechanism centers around the manipulation of topology through iterative refinement, providing a robust and adaptable solution for various search problems.

title: Title: Quantum-Inspired Machine Learning for Constraint Optimization
abstract: Quantum-inspired machine learning offers a promising avenue for addressing complex constraint satisfaction problems, particularly those exhibiting inherent non-linearity and sensitivity to initial conditions. This paper explores the application of quantum-inspired techniques – specifically entanglement-based heuristics – to enhance the performance of machine learning algorithms used for constraint satisfaction. We propose a novel algorithm designed to intelligently guide the optimization process, aiming to accelerate solution finding and improve performance compared to traditional methods. The core mechanism focuses on leveraging the inherent properties of quantum mechanics to provide a computational advantage. This research investigates the potential of incorporating these features into existing machine learning frameworks to achieve significant improvements in constraint satisfaction scenarios. The goal is to provide a practical and efficient approach for tackling problems demanding rapid and accurate solution discovery.

title: Non-Locality in Quantum Simulation – Creating Systems with Robustness to Measurement Errors
abstract: Quantum simulation is a rapidly advancing field with immense potential for understanding and manipulating quantum systems. However, the inherent non-locality of quantum mechanics presents significant challenges, particularly when simulating complex quantum environments. This paper explores the problem of measurement errors, which can significantly compromise the accuracy of quantum simulations. We propose a novel design for quantum simulation algorithms that explicitly incorporate mechanisms to mitigate these errors, focusing on a proactive error correction strategy. The core claim is that by incorporating this mechanism, we can create more robust simulations capable of accurately reproducing the underlying quantum system, even in the presence of unavoidable measurement errors.

title: InfoBank ScenarioPacks S1-S6: An Author-Validated Synthetic Dataset for Governed Multi-Document Question Answering
abstract: InfoBank ScenarioPacks S1–S6 is an author-validated synthetic dataset for evaluating governed, multi-document question answering over user-controlled documents. It contains six self-contained scenario packages with 41 synthetic PDF documents and 42 annotated queries covering furniture care and proof of purchase, television documentation and warranty, grocery-order aggregation, order and bank-statement reconciliation, warranty versus household insurance, and electric-vehicle charging with home solar equipment. The scenarios test single- and multi-document retrieval, object-specific distractor rejection, evidence-grounded answers and citations, temporal and quantitative reasoning, governed aggregation, clarification, and refusal when evidence or the required aggregation threshold is insufficient. Each ZIP includes source PDFs, runtime-safe query inputs, policy fixtures, retrieval contracts, separate human-validated reference annotations, tabular summaries, manifests, and SHA-256 checksums. Runtime inputs are separated from reference answers to reduce evaluation leakage. All documents are synthetic, written in English, and contain no real personal data, credentials, account data, or financial records. Although developed for InfoBank, the packages can be adapted to other permission-aware RAG and personal document-assistant implementations. Names appearing in technical identifiers or synthetic documents do not imply affiliation or endorsement. Version 2.0 extends the original InfoBank ScenarioPacks S1–S6 dataset with a flattened 42-case question–reference-answer catalog. An InfoBank implementation is avaliable at https://github.com/gkusper/InfoBank.

title: Enhanced Security of Quantum Key Distribution Protocols Based on Quantum Phase Decoherence
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to enhancing the security of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols by dynamically adjusting the estimation of quantum phase decoherence probability. Traditional QKD protocols often rely on static parameters, which limit their resilience against adaptive eavesdropping attacks. Our method leverages the real-time detection and mitigation of these attacks through the dynamic adjustment of decoherence probability estimation. Specifically, we introduce a feedback mechanism that monitors the estimated decoherence probability and adjusts key distribution parameters accordingly. This adaptive strategy provides a more robust defense against sophisticated attacks, ultimately improving the overall security of the QKD system. The core claim of this work is that dynamic adjustment of decoherence probability estimation can significantly bolster QKD security. The core mechanism relies on real-time attack detection and parameter adaptation. This approach represents a departure from the static parameter reliance of existing protocols, offering a proactive defense strategy.

title: Neural Network-Driven Program Generation
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to program generation utilizing simulated neural networks. The core concept involves training a neural network architecture to learn both algorithms and data patterns, subsequently enabling the automated creation of efficient code. Unlike traditional program synthesis methods, this research leverages the inherent pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks to directly translate high-level specifications into executable code. The system operates by mimicking human programming intuition and incorporating an algorithmic optimization process within the neural network structure. We explore the potential of this approach to accelerate software development and potentially discover novel algorithmic solutions. The architecture is designed to learn from both symbolic and numerical data, creating a robust and adaptable program generation system. This work presents a foundational framework for exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence and software engineering, offering a pathway toward intelligent code creation. The primary focus is on the conceptual design and theoretical underpinnings of the system, with future work planned to incorporate specific programming languages and evaluation methodologies.

title: A Distributed Proof System Based on Heterogeneous Computing Resources
abstract: This paper proposes a novel distributed proof system designed to leverage the parallel computing capabilities of heterogeneous computing resources, such as CPUs, GPUs, and FPGAs, for efficient execution of complex mathematical proofs. The system addresses the limitations of existing distributed computing systems, which are primarily optimized for general-purpose computation and lack the specialized optimization required for mathematical reasoning. The core mechanism involves decomposing mathematical proofs into smaller, independent sub-problems, assigning these sub-problems to different heterogeneous computing resources for parallel solution, and then integrating the results through a distributed collaboration framework. The system's architecture is predicated on a modular design, allowing for adaptability to diverse proof methodologies and computational resource availability. This approach significantly reduces the computational burden associated with complex proofs, offering the potential for substantially faster proof generation and verification times. The theoretical framework incorporates concepts from distributed systems, parallel computing, and formal verification, providing a robust foundation for the system's design and implementation. We present a conceptual overview and outline key components of the system, highlighting its potential impact on areas such as theorem proving, automated reasoning, and cryptographic protocol analysis. ---

title: High-Dimensional Non-Linear Geometry Topology Adaptive Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive optimization algorithm based on high-dimensional non-linear geometry topology. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with complex, high-dimensional data and require extensive parameter tuning. This algorithm leverages the inherent structure of geometric topologies to dynamically adjust optimization goals and parameters, leading to improved model optimization performance. We propose a "拓扑自适应优化" (Topology Adaptive Optimization) mechanism that dynamically connects the optimization process with the geometric topology of the problem, allowing for more effective model refinement. evidence.abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive optimization algorithm based on high-dimensional non-linear geometry topology. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with complex, high-dimensional data and require extensive parameter tuning. This algorithm leverages the inherent structure of geometric topologies to dynamically adjust optimization goals and parameters, leading to improved model optimization performance. We propose a "拓扑自适应优化" (Topology Adaptive Optimization) mechanism that dynamically connects the optimization process with the geometric topology of the problem, allowing for more effective model refinement. The proposed algorithm demonstrates improved results across a range of benchmark datasets, highlighting the potential of this approach to tackle challenging optimization problems.

title: Title: Dynamic Topology Synthesis for Neural Networks
abstract: Dynamic Topology Synthesis (DTS) represents a novel approach to neural network layer design, focusing on automated generation and fine-tuning of network topologies to optimize for performance and robustness. This paper introduces a method leveraging a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) to produce a "topology generator" capable of dynamically adapting to evolving data distributions. The core mechanism involves a continuous feedback loop, iteratively refining the network architecture through adversarial training, ultimately aiming to achieve superior generalization and efficiency. The resulting system demonstrates improved performance across a range of benchmark datasets, highlighting the potential of DTS to overcome limitations of traditional static architecture design.

title: Pigeons That Learn to Flank You: A Comparative Analysis Review of AI Techniques for NPCs and Dynamic Worlds
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of AI Techniques for NPCs and Dynamic Worlds in the context of Game Development. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of game AI and NPCs as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Game Development.

title: Quantum State Non-Linear Entanglement Computation
abstract: Quantum state non-linear entanglement computation is a burgeoning field with immense potential for advancing computational capabilities. This paper explores a novel computational model predicated on quantum entanglement, aiming to overcome the limitations of classical computation in processing complex non-linear quantum states. The core mechanism centers around leveraging entanglement's unique properties to facilitate efficient and highly complex operations on quantum states. This research focuses on the design of a quantum computing framework that utilizes entanglement to achieve computational speedups and offers a fundamentally different approach to problem-solving. The paper details the model's architecture, explores its potential for specific algorithms, and discusses its implications for future advancements in quantum computation.
