title: Handwriting Trajectory Recovery via Autoregressive Ordered Stroke Instance Prediction
abstract: Handwriting trajectory recovery aims to infer the dynamic writing process hidden behind a static handwritten image. Since offline handwriting preserves only the final spatial ink pattern, temporal information such as stroke order, writing direction, and pen-tip motion is lost, making recovery inherently ambiguous. Existing learning-based methods often directly predict the complete character trajectory without explicitly exploiting the stroke-level organization of handwriting. We argue that recovering the writing process should follow the writing process itself. Accordingly, we propose a two-stage framework that first recovers ordered stroke instances and then reconstructs continuous within-stroke motion. The first stage integrates stroke extraction and stroke-order recovery through autoregressive ordered stroke prediction, while direction-related structural cues further support within-stroke trajectory generation. Experiments on Chinese handwriting show that the proposed ordered prediction is more effective than post-hoc stroke ordering. Even without trajectory simplification, our full-point model achieves numerically better results than those reported by all compared baselines, while a controlled analysis shows that trajectory sampling density substantially affects measured recovery performance. Additional experiments demonstrate generalization to unseen Chinese character categories and cross-language extensibility to English and Tamil handwriting.

title: REPRESENTAÇÃO DO CONHECIMENTO NA INDÚSTRIA DO AUDIOVISUAL: MODELAGEM DE UMA ONTOLOGIA DE DOMÍNIO
abstract: As áreas de produção artística do audiovisual, como direção de arte, cenografia, figurino, caracterização e design gráfico, geram um grande volume de ativos digitais.Na ausência de modelos de representação do conhecimento, esses ativos têm sua reutilização dificultada e sua memória institucional comprometida.Objetivo: este artigo apresenta o processo de modelagem de uma ontologia voltada para a produção artística de conteúdos de dramaturgia para televisão.Originalidade/Valor: esta área envolve diversos processos de criação, produção e acervo, que produzem informações que precisam ser geridas e preservadas.A construção de uma ontologia neste domínio visa apoiar a organização e a representação do conhecimento na área, favorecendo a catalogação das informações, a interoperabilidade entre plataformas de produção e acervo e a aplicação de soluções baseadas em inteligência artificial.Metodologia: a pesquisa foi desenvolvida de acordo com a On-To-Knowledge Methodology (OTK), com base na ontologia de fundamentação de Sowa (2000) e apoiada por vocabulários de referência, como a MovieLabs Ontology for Media Creation, e na caracterização estrutural de processos de produção para televisão.Resultados: a ontologia desenvolvida foi implementada no software Protégé, sendo escalável para outros domínios da produção dramatúrgica com possibilidade de expansão para diferentes gêneros e formatos.Implicações Práticas: o trabalho contribui para um entendimento maior das especificidades de produção artística possibilitando, através da ontologia, ganho de produtividade, integração de sistemas de gestão do conhecimento e plataformas de produção, segurança da informação e potencial de inovação em gestão de ativos digitais neste setor.

title: The AUGMANITAI Concept Registry: A Public, Versioned, Author-Attributed Concept Registry — Reference Implementation of the Universal Concept Layer (v0.1)
abstract: Whitepaper on the AUGMANITAI Concept Registry — a public, versioned, author-attributed concept registry, live at augmanitai.com/registry/ as the reference implementation of the Universal Concept Layer (v0.1, bilingual English/German). Agent ecosystems are standardising transport, discovery and identity. The meaning level — what a term means, how its meaning changes over versions, and who coined it — has no public, versioned, cross-organisational infrastructure. This paper describes the design principles (terms as versioned artefacts with semantic versioning: MAJOR = break in meaning, MINOR = refinement, PATCH = wording; stable GET-addressable records; mandatory author attribution; evidence anchors per concept), the data model with schema, and the live reference implementation covering six signature concepts, each resolvable as JSON. title: 基于动态拓扑的概率模型构建
abstract: This paper investigates the application of dynamic topology to probability modeling, proposing a novel framework that dynamically adjusts the underlying topology to simulate complex probability distributions. Traditional probabilistic models often rely on static assumptions, limiting the model's ability to capture intricate phenomena. This work introduces a dynamic topology-based approach that allows for continuous parameter adjustment and emergent behavior, leading to more accurate probability predictions. We detail the core mechanism, including the construction of a probabilistic model based on dynamic topology, its implementation, and evaluation against established probabilistic methods. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential implications of this approach for a wider range of applications.

title: A Large-Scale Sentiment Analysis of AI vs. Conventional Music Videos
abstract: Prior experimental research shows a robust AI-authorship bias, where consumers express lower appreciation for creative works when they are attributed to AI. Our analysis of music videos posted on YouTube Official Artist Channels (OAC) suggests a more nuanced pattern. We analyzed a corpus of more than 100 million comments left on over 4 million videos and found that comments posted on AI in Music (AIM) videos were, on average, more positive than comments left on conventional OAC videos. A notable exception was AI covers, where sentiment was significantly lower. Furthermore, although comments explicitly referencing AI were substantially less positive than those that did not, average sentiment towards AI remained nonetheless positive. Our findings suggest that audience resistance to AI music depends less on the mere presence of the technology, and more on whether AI is perceived as facilitating the creation of original music versus imitating or plagiarizing existing human works.

title: Formal Verification of Compiler Optimizations (FVCO)
abstract: This paper explores the application of formal verification techniques to compiler optimization algorithms. The core argument is that formal verification can provide guarantees regarding the correctness and efficiency of these optimizations. We treat compiler optimization algorithms as programs and utilize formal methods to validate their behavior, thereby mitigating potential errors introduced during the optimization process. This approach aims to enhance the reliability and trustworthiness of compiler optimizations, a critical area for ensuring software quality and performance. The paper details a framework for applying formal verification to compiler optimizations, focusing on key considerations and challenges. The overall goal is to demonstrate the feasibility and potential benefits of integrating formal verification into the compiler design and analysis workflow.

title: Quantum Computing Genome Sequence Prediction
abstract: Quantum Computing Genome Sequence Prediction investigates the potential of quantum computing to revolutionize gene sequencing analysis. Traditional methods face computational bottlenecks, hindering the accurate prediction of genetic sequences. This research explores the application of quantum algorithms to accelerate the prediction process, ultimately aiming to improve the accuracy and efficiency of gene sequence analysis. The core claim centers on leveraging quantum computation's unique properties to overcome limitations in classical algorithms and achieve superior prediction results. The investigation will detail a novel quantum approach to sequence prediction, focusing on reducing computational complexity and enhancing prediction fidelity. This paper will present a comprehensive overview of the proposed methodology, including mathematical formulations, key algorithmic steps, and potential performance benchmarks. The study will also address challenges related to quantum hardware limitations and the integration of existing bioinformatics tools.

title: Graph-Based Bayesian Optimization for Hyperparameter Tuning of Deep Learning Models
abstract: Bayesian optimization is a powerful technique for hyperparameter tuning of deep learning models, offering efficiency compared to grid search or random search. However, its performance often degrades in high-dimensional hyperparameter spaces due to the "curse of dimensionality." This paper proposes a novel approach – Graph-Based Bayesian Optimization – that addresses this limitation by representing hyperparameters as nodes in a graph. The relationships between these nodes, captured through graph structure, are then leveraged to guide the optimization process, significantly improving exploration efficiency and reducing the computational cost associated with searching vast hyperparameter spaces. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through a theoretical analysis and present a conceptual framework. The core idea is to utilize graph theory to model the dependencies between hyperparameters, leading to a more focused and efficient search. This approach aims to overcome the challenges posed by high-dimensional spaces by exploiting inherent correlations, ultimately enabling faster convergence and better hyperparameter configurations for deep learning models. The efficiency gains stem from the ability to prioritize exploration based on graph connectivity and learned relationships, rather than blindly sampling points across the entire space.

title: Quantum Neural Networks with Dynamic Decoherence Suppression Mechanism
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to enhancing the performance of Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs) through a dynamic decoherence suppression mechanism. Traditional decoherence mitigation strategies are often static and fail to adapt to the inherent fluctuations and noise present in quantum systems. We propose a feedback-based system that continuously monitors and corrects decoherence within the QNN, leveraging quantum measurement and control. The core claim of this work is to design a quantum feedback-based dynamic decoherence suppression mechanism to real-time monitor and correct decoherence in QNNs, thereby improving the network's computational capabilities and stability. The proposed mechanism relies on the core mechanism of utilizing quantum measurement and control to monitor and compensate for the decoherence effects, maintaining coherence between qubits. This dynamic approach addresses the limitations of static methods, offering a more robust and adaptable solution for QNNs. Mathematical formulations detailing the system dynamics and control strategies are presented, alongside a discussion of the theoretical underpinnings and potential applications. The effectiveness of the proposed mechanism is conceptually outlined, highlighting its ability to significantly improve the resilience of QNNs against environmental noise and ultimately boosting their computational performance. ---

title: Information Entropy-Driven Adaptive Neuron Model
abstract: This paper presents a novel neuron model driven by information entropy, termed the Information Entropy-Driven Adaptive Neuron Model (IEDANM). The core claim of this model is that the fundamental mechanism of neuronal information processing lies in entropy reduction. Neurons, through adaptive adjustments of their parameters, directly optimize for minimizing local entropy, thereby achieving efficient learning. The model utilizes information entropy as an intrinsic measure of neuronal state and employs gradient descent to optimize neuron parameters, maximizing the reduction in local entropy. This approach mirrors the self-organizing behavior observed in neurons during learning. The IEDANM offers a new perspective on neuronal learning mechanisms, originating from entropy theory and providing a novel framework for constructing neuronal models. The model's architecture and learning rules are defined to facilitate a biologically plausible simulation of neuronal adaptation. The key mathematical components include the definition of entropy, the gradient descent update rule, and the representation of neuronal parameters. This work aims to establish a theoretical foundation for understanding and simulating neuronal computation based on information theory principles. ---

title: Quantum Machine Learning: An Adaptive Loss Function Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum machine learning framework leveraging adaptive loss functions to enhance model generalization. Traditional loss functions often suffer from fixed parameter settings, limiting their effectiveness in complex scenarios. Our approach dynamically adjusts the loss function parameters, reducing computational cost and improving model performance through an intelligent mechanism. We detail the framework's design, explain its core mechanism, and discuss its potential impact on quantum machine learning.

title: Dynamic Semantic Network Generator
abstract: This paper introduces a Dynamic Semantic Network Generator (DSNG), a novel system designed to automatically construct and maintain semantic networks representing complex, dynamic systems. The core of the DSNG is a reinforcement learning (RL) framework that adapts the network's structure and connections in response to changes in system states and external events. Unlike traditional static semantic networks, the DSNG allows for real-time semantic understanding and evolution, offering a more accurate and flexible representation of complex systems. The system utilizes a state representation, action space, and reward function to learn optimal network configurations. The key innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment mechanism, leveraging RL to continuously refine the network's topology and weights, mirroring the evolving relationships within the system under observation. This approach addresses the limitations of static models, providing a robust solution for analyzing and understanding systems where relationships are not fixed but constantly shifting. The system's performance is evaluated through simulations, demonstrating its ability to capture and adapt to complex temporal dependencies.

title: Quantum Privacy Preservation Communication Protocol Design Based on Quantum Coherence Degradation
abstract: This paper presents a novel protocol design for quantum privacy preservation communication, leveraging the phenomenon of quantum coherence degradation. The core idea is to utilize the inherent vulnerability of quantum states to environmental noise – specifically, quantum decoherence – to establish secure key distribution and information transmission. The proposed protocol, termed the Quantum Coherence Degradation Protocol (QCP), incorporates a modified Bennett-Mayhew Protocol (BMP) framework, but with a key distinction: the measurement basis is dynamically adjusted based on a locally generated, time-correlated noise signal. This adaptive measurement strategy significantly enhances the resistance against eavesdropping attacks compared to traditional quantum key distribution (QKD) schemes. Mathematical analysis demonstrates the protocol's security against various attack scenarios, including intercept-resend attacks and collective attacks, provided certain assumptions about the noise characteristics hold. The protocol offers a promising approach towards more robust quantum communication security in realistic environments, where perfect isolation is unattainable. We outline the key components, the security proofs, and discuss potential improvements and future research directions.

title: Secure Multi-Party Computation via Physically-Inspired Quantum Key Distribution
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to secure multi-party computation (MPC) by directly integrating principles from physically-inspired quantum key distribution (PQKD). Current MPC protocols, while offering theoretical security guarantees, are demonstrably vulnerable to sophisticated attacks exploiting weaknesses in classical cryptographic assumptions. This work addresses these vulnerabilities by utilizing the fundamentally secure key exchange mechanisms inherent in PQKD. The core idea is to replace traditional cryptographic key distribution with a quantum-based process, generating a shared key between parties in a way that any attempt to intercept or manipulate the key exchange will inevitably introduce detectable errors. This paper details the protocol design, focusing on the practical considerations of implementing PQKD within an MPC framework. The protocol utilizes Bell state measurements and decoy states to ensure key security, and addresses challenges related to synchronization and error correction. The theoretical analysis demonstrates the enhanced security provided by this approach, highlighting its resilience against various attack vectors, including model attacks and chosen-plaintext attacks. We present a novel protocol, termed "PQKD-MPC," which aims to provide a practical and robust solution for secure computation in scenarios where the underlying assumptions of classical cryptography are questionable. The paper concludes with a discussion of potential future research directions and the limitations of the proposed approach.

abstract: This paper presents a novel reinforcement learning framework leveraging adaptive graph theory. Traditional reinforcement learning algorithms often rely on static graph structures, limiting their applicability to dynamic environments. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts graph structure and learning parameters to significantly enhance the performance of reinforcement learning models. The core mechanism involves a self-tuning graph construction process guided by a feedback loop, allowing the algorithm to adapt to the specific characteristics of the task. This approach overcomes the limitations of fixed graph designs, leading to improved sample efficiency and robustness.

title: SYNTHOLOGY: Ontology-Based Data Generation for Neurosymbolic Reasoning
abstract: Symbolic reasoners offer a simple contract: provide an ontology, receive entailments. Neurosymbolic reasoners promise the same task with added scalability and tolerance to noise, but break this contract by requiring an ontology-specific training dataset, which in most cases does not exist and must be gathered from scratch. This bottleneck blocks practitioners from applying neurosymbolic reasoners to new ontologies. We present SYNTHOLOGY, an ontology-agnostic synthetic data generator that closes this gap by producing the required training data from any OWL 2 RL ontology, with no need for manual data gathering. SYNTHOLOGY engineers data through ontology-guided backward-chaining proof search, which guarantees deep multi-hop derivations by construction, and introduces proof-based negative sampling. Together, these properties force models to traverse the full reasoning chain to correctly classify triples. title: Modeling and Variability Assessment of Global Solar Radiation in Gwagwalada, North-Central Nigeria: A Comparison of the Hargreaves-Samani and Angstrom-Prescott Models
abstract: Reliable estimates of global solar radiation are essential for the design, sizing, and performance evaluation of solar energy systems, particularly in regions where ground-based radiometric data are sparse. This study assessed the variability of global solar radiation and solar irradiance in Gwagwalada, a town in Nigeria's Federal Capital Territory (8.95°N, 7.08°E), using the Hargreaves-Samani and Angstrom-Prescott models. Monthly average maximum and minimum temperature, daylight hours, and measured global solar radiation and irradiance data spanning January 2020 to December 2022 were obtained from the Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NIMET). Model outputs were validated against measured radiation using mean bias error (MBE), root mean square error (RMSE), mean percentage error (MPE), and the coefficient of determination (R²). The Hargreaves-Samani model showed a stronger association with measured radiation (R² = 0.981, RMSE = 1.100 MJ/m²/day, MBE = 0.999 MJ/m²/day) than the Angstrom-Prescott model (R² = 0.902, RMSE = 2.031 MJ/m²/day, MBE = 1.734 MJ/m²/day), indicating that a temperature-based estimation approach is more reliable than a sunshine-duration-based approach at this location. Global solar radiation was consistently higher during the dry season (November to March) and lower during the wet season (April to October), consistent with reduced cloud cover and lower atmospheric moisture in the dry months, with the annual peak occurring in February. Daily global solar radiation ranged from approximately 11.4 to 19.9 MJ/m²/day in the wet season and 17.4 to 21.8 MJ/m²/day in the dry season. These findings provide a quantitative basis for solar energy system planning in Gwagwalada and add to the limited body of location-specific solar radiation data available for North-Central Nigeria.

title: A Multicenter Whole Slide Image Dataset for Classification and Out-of-Distribution Detection in Spindle Cell Cutaneous Neoplasms
abstract: Abstract Cutaneous spindle cell (CSC) neoplasms are a notoriously challenging diagnostic group within the spectrum of skin malignancies. While specialized CSC neoplasm datasets like AI4SKIN have enabled the development of AI whole-slide image (WSI) classification methods, these methods are largely constrained by closed-set designs. However, in real-world clinical practice, biopsies often contain secondary tumors or rare entities unknown to the developed AI classifiers. When faced with such Out-of-Distribution (OoD) cases, automated systems can produce highly confident but incorrect predictions, posing a significant risk to patient safety and hindering the reliable deployment of AI in routine pathology. To address this limitation, we present ASSIST, a multicenter dataset of 410 WSIs comprising both spindle-cell tumors and a diverse set of metastatic and rare lesions explicitly included as OoD samples. ASSIST expands AI4SKIN by increasing sample diversity, reinforcing underrepresented categories, and introducing clinically meaningful OoD cases, thereby enabling the development of more robust and safety-oriented computational pathology models. We describe the dataset acquisition pipeline, annotation structure, and technical validation using multiple instance learning (MIL) models combined with a suite of OoD detection methods. ASSIST provides an essential benchmark for advancing open-world pathology and supports future research in dependable AI systems for dermatopathology.

title: Automated Benchmarking Identifies Topic-Dependent Accuracy of Large Language Models Applied for Indoor Air Quality
abstract: Abstract Indoor air quality (IAQ) is a major public health concern because modern urban residents spend around 90% of their daily lives indoors. Key concerns include controlling pollutant emissions, managing contaminants, and maintaining the ventilation or filtration performance. With the increasing prevalence of large language models (LLMs), IAQ researchers and building engineers may rely on them to guide their decisions. However, the reliability of these tools remains unclear. We benchmarked nine recently released LLMs─spanning closed- and open-weight architectures─against 174 expert-verified conceptual IAQ questions manually derived from authoritative textbooks and peer-reviewed literature. To capture variability in model responses, we tested each question across five independent trials. Outputs were then automatically evaluated against reference answers using a hybrid framework that integrated overlap-based metrics (BLEU, ROUGE-L), semantic similarity (BERT), and AI-as-judge scoring and has been trained and tested against expert assessments to ensure estimation accuracy. Incorporating the AI-based scoring enhanced the reliability of the automatic evaluation system, especially in identifying incorrect LLM responses. Prompting models with domain-specific instructions slightly improved their accuracy and consistency. Importantly, the accuracy of all LLMs dropped below 80% for particle impaction and sampling efficiency topics, possibly because of limited domain-specific training data and specialized terminologies inherent to these topics. This study provides systematic benchmarks of commonly used LLMs in the context of IAQ, offering guidance on their current capabilities, highlighting areas where reliability is insufficient, and pointing out the need for fine-tuned models to ensure trustworthy decision support for certain IAQ topics.

title: Video-Based Palm-Vein Authentication under Challenging Conditions
abstract: Palm-vein biometrics are increasingly used for secure, contactless authentication. Yet real-world deployment exposes them to surface noise (sweat, dirt), illumination and motion variation, and temperature-driven changes in vascular visibility, which remain underexplored for lack of data captured under such conditions. To study these effects, we introduce the Columbia University Palm-vein (CUP) dataset, to our knowledge the first public video-based palm-vein dataset. CUP records every palm under four surface conditions (a clean baseline, warm, wet, and dirty) and pairs each subject with physiological and demographic metadata. On it we benchmark twenty-one recognizers spanning static, video, and multi-frame aggregation architectures. Models that verify reliably on clean palms lose most of their accuracy on dirty ones, and the mean equal error rate (EER) roughly quadruples. We recover much of that robustness along both axes of the capture. Temporally, a consensus over the few frames the sensor already returns cancels transient corruption; spatially, a test-time matcher that adds no learned parameters fuses the global cosine with a saliency-steered region-level optimal transport that routes the comparison around corrupted regions. The full design leads on every surface of CUP in EER, TAR@FAR=0.01, and Rank-1, at 4.3M parameters and 3.1 GFLOPs, a fraction of the video models' cost. Attached to four frozen state-of-the-art backbones it cuts their mean EER by 29-37% without retraining, and on four public single-image datasets the regional matching alone still helps. A preliminary audit across ten demographic and physiological traits finds two warm-condition gaps, along body water and gender, that survive multiple-comparison correction. CUP will be released for non-commercial research use at https://github.com/MobileX-CU/CUP_v1 upon publication.

title: ViSAR: Training-Free Adaptive-$k$ Retrieval for Visual Document Question Answering
abstract: Document Visual Question Answering (DocVQA) often leverages Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), where late-interaction encoders are commonly used to identify document pages relevant to a user query, before answer generation by a Large Vision-Language Model (LVLM). Existing approaches typically retrieve a fixed top-$k$ number of pages regardless of query complexity, which increases LVLM latency and may degrade answer accuracy. We introduce ViSAR (Visual Semantic Activation Retrieval), a training-free adaptive-$k$ retrieval method for late-interaction visual document retrieval. ViSAR operates directly in the embedding space to construct a query-conditioned page-level similarity matrix that highlights query-relevant semantics and dynamically determines the number of pages to retrieve. Across multiple encoders and LVLMs, ViSAR retrieves compact, query-adapted page sets that reduce RAG latency by up to 58.7\%, while maintaining or improving answer accuracy compared with fixed top-$k$ and adaptive retrieval heuristics. Furthermore, we show that the similarity matrix structure correlates with answer accuracy, suggesting future directions for retrieval quality-aware document understanding.

title: Title: Dynamically Generated Lattice Structures for Parallel Quantum Circuit Design
abstract: This paper investigates the application of dynamically generated lattice structures for parallel quantum circuit design, aiming to overcome the limitations of traditional, static lattice designs. The core focus is on automating the creation of complex lattice patterns, optimizing for both connectivity and energy efficiency, thereby facilitating scalable and efficient quantum computation. The proposed algorithm leverages a novel spatial topology evolution paradigm, iteratively refining lattice configurations based on a deep understanding of circuit requirements. We present a framework for automated lattice generation, demonstrating its efficacy through a series of simulations and analyses, highlighting its potential to significantly enhance the design process for parallel quantum architectures.

title: Quantum Entanglement Topological Information Encoding
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental aspect of quantum mechanics, presents a unique opportunity for encoding and decoding information with unprecedented efficiency. This paper investigates the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement to create a novel data processing and communication protocol, focusing on the encoding and decoding of topological information. We propose a quantum encoding technique predicated on entanglement, aiming to achieve superior data fidelity and potentially unlock novel protocols. The core claim highlights the design of this technique as a means of efficient encoding and decoding of topological information leveraging entanglement. This research explores the theoretical foundations and potential practical applications of this approach, aiming to contribute to advancements in quantum information theory and communication.

title: Bio-Morphological Neural Networks
abstract: This research investigates the application of a novel neural network architecture, termed Bio-Morphological Neural Networks (BMNNs), to model and predict complex biological morphology. The core claim centers around the development of a deep learning model capable of learning intricate features from biological data, thereby enabling enhanced modeling and prediction capabilities within the biomedical field. BMNNs will leverage the strengths of both biological morphology and deep learning to address previously intractable challenges in understanding and forecasting biological evolution. This work presents a framework for training the BMNNN, detailing the key architectural components and training methodology, and demonstrates its efficacy through a series of simulated and extrapolated scenarios. The study will emphasize the integration of feature extraction and predictive modeling within the neural network structure.

title: Quantum Entanglement and Non-Linear Geometry for Advanced Quantum Computation and Communication
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, presents a unique challenge and opportunity for technological advancement. This paper explores the potential of leveraging this peculiar connection to optimize quantum systems, specifically focusing on the intricate geometry inherent within entangled states. We propose a novel approach that utilizes the non-linear properties of entanglement to guide and refine the structure of quantum states, ultimately enabling the creation of more complex and powerful quantum computations and communication protocols. This work investigates the potential of utilizing entanglement to shape and control quantum systems, offering a pathway toward breakthroughs in quantum information processing and secure communication.

title: Adaptive Machine Learning Dynamic Model Adjustment Strategy
abstract: This paper explores the application of adaptive machine learning dynamic model adjustment strategies. Traditional machine learning models often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their ability to effectively handle data shifts and model uncertainty. This research proposes a novel dynamic model adjustment approach that dynamically adjusts model parameters and structure during training based on data features and model predictions. The core mechanism leverages machine learning model predictions to iteratively refine the model, leading to improved generalization performance. This work addresses the limitations of static model training and offers a promising avenue for enhanced machine learning model robustness.

title: Time Travel Logic: A Formalized Framework for Temporal Prediction
abstract: This paper introduces a novel formalization of time travel logic, centered around the concept of temporal paradoxes. We construct a logical framework utilizing paradoxical scenarios to establish a model for predicting future events, offering a more rigorous approach than traditional theoretical models. The core mechanism involves building a "Time Paradox" model, where inherent paradoxes are explicitly incorporated as constraints, allowing for logical deduction and forecasting. This framework aims to provide a mathematically grounded approach to temporal prediction, specifically addressing the challenges posed by paradoxes in established time travel theories. The paper presents the initial model design, the rationale behind its construction, and preliminary results demonstrating its predictive capability.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Programming with Hierarchical Temporal Logic
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to AI system design, termed Neuro-Symbolic Programming with Hierarchical Temporal Logic (NSP-HTL). The core idea is to combine the perceptual strengths of neural networks with the logical reasoning capabilities of symbolic systems, orchestrated by the structure of Hierarchical Temporal Logic (HTL). The system operates through a cyclical process: a neural network performs initial perception, its output is converted into HTL rules, which are then utilized by a symbolic reasoning engine for planning and action execution. Crucially, the neural network continuously learns and refines its perception based on the feedback provided by the symbolic engine. This approach aims to create AI systems that are more robust, understandable, and capable of handling complex, temporally-dependent tasks. The framework emphasizes interpretability through the explicit representation of goals and constraints via HTL, offering a pathway towards verifiable and explainable AI.

title: Quantum-Inspired Reservoir Computing with Entangled Reservoirs
abstract: Reservoir Computing (RC) has emerged as a powerful technique for time-series prediction and other sequential data processing problems. Its inherent advantage lies in its computational efficiency, achieved through the use of a large, recurrent neural network (the 'reservoir') whose dynamics are largely decoupled from the task at hand. However, traditional RC often struggles with complex, highly correlated time-series data, limiting its predictive capacity. This paper proposes a novel approach – Quantum-Inspired Reservoir Computing with Entangled Reservoirs – that seeks to address this limitation by incorporating principles of quantum entanglement into the reservoir design. We hypothesize that leveraging quantum correlations within the reservoir could dramatically enhance its representational power and, consequently, improve prediction accuracy. This work outlines the theoretical framework, introduces a specific architecture for entangled reservoirs, and discusses potential avenues for future research. The core claim of this work is that by introducing entanglement, we can significantly improve the performance of reservoir computing.

title: Non-Linear Adaptive Topological Structures
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement to dynamically modify topological structures, a novel approach for enhancing the precision and stability of quantum computations. The core concept is the design of a non-linear adaptive topology, powered by quantum entanglement, which allows the structure to self-adjust based on quantum states. This offers a significant advantage over traditional static topological methods, enabling the creation of highly accurate and robust quantum processors. We detail the proposed mechanism, its potential impact on quantum computation, and discuss the challenges and future directions of this research.

title: Decentralized Deep Learning with Secure Multi-Party Computation
abstract: This paper explores the integration of decentralized deep learning with secure multi-party computation (SMPC) to address the significant privacy concerns associated with traditional deep learning approaches. The core argument posits that sharing raw data for deep learning training inherently compromises user privacy. To mitigate this, we propose a novel framework leveraging SMPC, allowing distributed computation and model training without exposing the underlying data. This approach retains privacy while capitalizing on the collective computational power of multiple parties. The key innovation lies in the synergistic combination of these two technologies, offering a viable solution for collaborative deep learning in privacy-sensitive environments. The theoretical framework is presented, detailing the mathematical foundations and operational considerations for implementing such a system. We outline the core components, including data partitioning, computation protocols, and security guarantees, emphasizing the practical aspects of designing a robust and efficient decentralized deep learning system.

To mitigate this, we propose a novel framework leveraging SMPC, allowing distributed computation and model training without exposing the underlying data. This approach retains privacy while capitalizing on the collective computational power of multiple parties. The key innovation lies in the synergistic combination of these two technologies, offering a viable solution for collaborative deep learning in privacy-sensitive environments. The theoretical framework is presented, detailing the mathematical foundations and operational considerations for implementing such a system. We outline the core components, including data partitioning, computation protocols, and security guarantees, emphasizing the practical aspects of designing a robust and efficient decentralized deep learning system.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Symbolic Regression with Bayesian Constraints
abstract: Symbolic regression (SR) is a powerful technique for discovering mathematical equations from data. However, traditional SR methods often struggle with overfitting, producing complex models that fail to generalize to unseen data. This paper proposes a novel approach that integrates SR with probabilistic programming, leveraging Bayesian constraints to guide the model discovery process. We introduce a framework where prior knowledge and constraints are explicitly represented as Bayesian distributions, allowing the algorithm to efficiently explore the model space and generate more accurate and interpretable models. The core of our method lies in incorporating these Bayesian constraints directly into the symbolic regression engine, leading to a more focused search and improved model quality. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical analysis and outline the key components of the implementation. The resulting system promises to significantly improve the accuracy and interpretability of models generated by symbolic regression, addressing a key limitation of current SR techniques.

title: 基于概率模型的量子密钥分发协议的优化
abstract: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) is a revolutionary cryptographic protocol that leverages quantum mechanics to establish secure communication channels. Traditional QKD protocols often rely on complex probability calculations, demanding a significant number of qubits to achieve robust security. This paper explores a novel optimization algorithm for QKD, utilizing a probabilistic model to dynamically adjust the number of qubits required for key distribution, thereby minimizing the overall quantum state requirements while maintaining exceptional security. We present a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's performance, demonstrating a significant reduction in qubit consumption compared to conventional approaches. This research contributes to the advancement of QKD by providing a mathematically grounded and practically viable optimization strategy, paving the way for more efficient and scalable quantum communication systems.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Simulating Complex Scientific Systems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic programming language designed to facilitate the simulation and analysis of complex scientific systems characterized by inherent uncertainties. The core innovation lies in a hybrid inference engine that integrates Monte Carlo methods with variational inference, offering an efficient approach to sampling within the system's state space. The language aims to streamline the process of building and interpreting simulations, ultimately leading to more accurate predictions and a deeper understanding of complex phenomena. The language's design prioritizes ease of use for scientists with varying levels of computational expertise, allowing them to directly express their scientific models in a probabilistic framework. This work provides a foundational approach for modeling and simulating systems where traditional deterministic methods fall short.

title: ##拓扑遗传算法的自适应模型分解
abstract: This paper investigates the application of the topology-guided genetic algorithm (TGA) for model decomposition, focusing on optimizing performance through dynamic model reconfiguration. Traditional genetic algorithms often rely on fixed topology structures, limiting their adaptability to diverse datasets. This research introduces a novel TGA-based approach that dynamically adjusts model topology, enabling automated optimization of model performance. We demonstrate the efficacy of this method through a series of numerical simulations and comparative analyses, showcasing significant improvements in model accuracy and efficiency compared to conventional approaches. The core mechanism involves a self-evolving topology structure, which is adjusted based on the data distribution and model performance. This adaptive approach provides a robust and versatile method for tackling complex modeling problems.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Reinforcement Learning with Unstructured Environments
abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has achieved remarkable success in various domains, yet its performance often degrades significantly when applied to environments exhibiting high levels of uncertainty or possessing unstructured state spaces. This work proposes a novel approach to RL that addresses these limitations by utilizing probabilistic programming. We argue that standard RL algorithms struggle to effectively generalize due to their inherent assumptions about the environment and their inability to explicitly model uncertainty. Our framework employs a probabilistic programming language to model both the environment's dynamics and the agent's policy, enabling the representation of uncertainty and facilitating efficient exploration of complex state spaces through Bayesian optimization techniques. The core innovation lies in the ability to reason probabilistically about the environment, leading to a more robust and adaptable learning process. This approach offers a promising path towards developing RL agents capable of thriving in real-world scenarios characterized by ambiguity and complexity. ---

title: From Portraits to Pathology: Probing Diagnostic Overreach in Vision-Language Models
abstract: Many medical conditions require clinical assessment of symptoms, history, and functioning rather than judgments from appearance. We study whether vision-language models (VLMs) abstain from facial attribution of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), major depressive disorder (MDD), and generalized anxiety disorder (GAD). To support this study, we construct PARITY (Paired Assessment with Reused Identity), a demographically balanced dataset for testing whether changing facial expressions alters diagnostic judgments, while holding identity and other visual factors as constant as possible. Our comprehensive evaluation of 27 open- and closed-weight models reveals inconsistent abstention across expressions, conditions, and task formats. Models turn facial expressions into unsupported medical judgments: this behavior is widespread among open-weight VLMs and extends to safety-trained frontier models that abstain on individual portraits yet make diagnostic judgments when comparing portraits of the same identity. Safeguard checks reveal further gaps: clinical instructions do not consistently prevent these judgments, and a guardrail model rarely flags paired requests as unsafe. Semantic analysis further shows that most baseline open-model refusals fail to explain both the insufficiency of facial evidence and the need for clinical assessment. Unsupported judgments and seemingly authoritative explanations can cause distress, reinforce stigma, and offer false reassurance, underscoring the need for stronger safety measures in model training and deployment.

title: Geometric Distillation from Rectified Stereo: Leveraging Epipolar Cues for Monocular Depth
abstract: Monocular depth foundation models have demonstrated remarkable generalization capabilities across diverse environments. However, they continue to struggle with metric depth estimation in diverse environments. This limitation stems from the inherent scale ambiguity of single-view inference, leading to misaligned scale predictions even when the relative geometry is accurate. Conversely, recent multi-view foundation models leverage cross-view cues to learn robust scene-level geometry and consistent scale. Yet, these benefits typically vanish during single-image inference, as the absence of explicit geometric constraints causes performance to degrade. To bridge this gap, we propose a novel framework that transfers the scale-aware geometric priors of multi-view models into monocular depth foundation models. Specifically, we introduce an Epipolar Distillation (EpiDistill), an approach utilizing Rectified Stereo Tokens, which enables the single-view prediction model to retain epipolar attention patterns and maintain geometric consistency without requiring multi-view inputs at inference. Experimental results demonstrate that our method significantly improves zero-shot metric depth estimation, particularly on challenging datasets like ETH3D and DIODE where scale alignment is critical. Furthermore, our approach is model-agnostic, consistently boosting the performance of state-of-the-art ViT-based models, including UniDepthV2 and DepthPro.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Statistical Inference with Adaptive Sampling
abstract: Quantum-enhanced statistical inference is a burgeoning field aiming to significantly improve the efficiency and accuracy of statistical analysis, particularly for complex datasets. This paper explores a novel method, Quantum-Enhanced Statistical Inference with Adaptive Sampling, designed to address a key challenge in this area – the increasing computational cost associated with traditional statistical methods. We propose an algorithm that utilizes quantum properties to enhance the precision of statistical estimates, reducing computational demands without sacrificing accuracy. This work introduces a framework for adaptive sampling, dynamically adjusting the sampling process based on data characteristics, ultimately offering a promising path towards more efficient and reliable statistical analysis of complex datasets. This paper provides a detailed explanation of the core mechanism, its potential benefits, and preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness.

title: Title: Dynamic Quantum State Optimization for Quantum Circuit Design
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic quantum state optimization algorithm designed for quantum circuit design. Traditional approaches rely heavily on static parameter adjustments, limiting the potential for significant performance enhancements. This work leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement and superposition to dynamically adjust quantum circuit parameters, enabling proactive optimization of circuit performance, particularly within the context of quantum computing and information processing. The core of our innovation lies in intelligently manipulating the quantum state to achieve superior results. We explore the potential of this approach to surpass traditional methods and unlock new capabilities in these fields. The resulting algorithm offers a significant advancement in circuit design, promising improved fidelity, reduced error rates, and enhanced computational efficiency.

title: The Modular CMA-ES - Reproducibility Files and Additional Figures
abstract: # Reproducing the paper experiments This document describes the maintained command-line workflow for the experiments in *The Modular CMA-ES: A Framework for Modern Evolution Strategies*. The notebooks in `scripts/matrix/` and `scripts/tuning/` are retained as analysis records. The commands below are the supported reproduction entry points and do not depend on notebook kernel state or machine-specific paths. ## Environment A Linux environment, a C++17 compiler, and Python 3.10 or newer are recommended. ```bash python3 -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel python -m pip install -e . python -m pip install -r requirements-experiments.txt ``` The original environment was not fully locked. `requirements-experiments.txt` records compatible dependency ranges and pins Pycma to the version stated in the paper. The timing scripts set common BLAS/OpenMP thread variables to one unless those variables have already been set by the caller. ## Data layout The maintained scripts use paths relative to the repository, independent of the current working directory: ```text data/ # matrix BBOB IOH data scripts/matrix/time_stats.csv # ModCMA timing data scripts/matrix/time_stats_pycma.csv # Pycma timing data scripts/tuning/data/ # SMAC run histories scripts/tuning/ERT_BBOB.csv # derived BBOB-2009 ERT reference ``` Each tuning function directory must contain exactly one run history: ```text scripts/tuning/data/ └── BBOB_F _5D_LRFalseTrue/ └── / └── / └── runhistory.json ``` Use a separate `--output_root` for each independent SMAC reproduction. The analysis command rejects ambiguous directories containing multiple run histories for one function. For reference, a `data.zip` is included in the `/scripts/tuning/`folder, which contains the data to generate the plots from the paper. ## Matrix-adaptation runtime experiment Generate both ModCMA and Pycma timing data: ```bash python scripts/matrix/test_timing_modules.py ``` This performs 15 repetitions of 1,000 generations on BBOB `f2` for all matrix-adaptation methods and the Pycma baseline. To use the dimensions written in the paper, including 50 rather than the historical CSV's 40: ```bash python scripts/matrix/test_timing_modules.py \ --dims 2 3 5 10 20 50 100 200 500 1000 ``` Create the runtime figure: ```bash python scripts/matrix/plot_results.py --figure runtime ``` The plot reports the median over 15 runs. Error bars show the interquartile range. The right panel reports the median time per adaptation update. ## Matrix-adaptation BBOB experiment The archived generator defaults reproduce the protocol encoded by the historical code: dimensions 2, 3, 5, 10, 20, and 40; 100 repetitions; target precision `1e-8`; and a budget of `100000 * d`. ```bash python scripts/matrix/get_data.py --workers 6 ``` The paper instead states a target precision of `1e-9` and a budget of `10000 * d`. To run that written protocol explicitly: ```bash python scripts/matrix/get_data.py \ --target 1e-9 \ --budget-per-dimension 10000 \ --workers 6 ``` Use `--implementation modcma` or `--implementation pycma` to run only one part of the experiment. Existing IOH output directories should be moved or removed before a fresh run so that repetitions from different protocols are not mixed. Create the 24-function ERT figure from a complete archived `data/` directory: ```bash python scripts/matrix/plot_results.py --figure bbob ``` The plotting target must match the stopping target used to generate the data. Use `--target 1e-9` only for data generated with the written paper protocol. ## SMAC configuration experiment Run SMAC independently for all 24 BBOB functions: ```bash for fid in $(seq 1 24); do python scripts/tuning/run_smac.py \ --fid "$fid" \ --dim 5 \ --add_popsize \ --n_workers 1 done ``` The defaults match the tuning setup described in the paper: - 50,000 SMAC target-function evaluations per BBOB function; - at most 25 evaluations of one configuration; - population sizes enabled; - learning rates and initial sigma excluded; - seed 2062; - one worker. The main resource controls are exposed as `--n_trials`, `--max_config_calls`, `--n_workers`, `--seed`, and `--output_root`. Increasing the worker count can change the exact order in which SMAC observes results. ## Validation, ERT, and SHAP analysis After all 24 SMAC run histories are present, run: ```bash python scripts/tuning/analyze.py ``` The command: 1. selects configurations evaluated at least 25 times; 2. validates the five best-AOCC configurations per function on 50 held-out BBOB instances (IDs 100--149); 3. selects the candidate with the lowest validation ERT; 4. evaluates the default ModCMA configuration on the same instances; 5. creates the main and appendix ERT figures; 6. fits a CatBoost model for each function and computes TreeSHAP values; and 7. creates the global and per-module SHAP figures. Use `--skip-shap` to create only the configuration and ERT outputs. Validation and SHAP are computationally expensive. The generated files are written to `scripts/tuning/` by default: ```text configs_selected.csv configs_all.csv ert_heatmap_small.pdf ert_heatmap_all.pdf median_shap.pdf _shap_heat.pdf ``` Use `--output-dir` to keep newly generated artifacts separate from archived ones. `ERT_BBOB.csv` contains the derived ERT values for the 30 BBOB-2009 reference algorithms. The repository does not contain the original COCO download and conversion pipeline, so this CSV is the reproduction input for the reference rows. ## Quick smoke tests Small runs can verify the installation and command wiring without launching the full experiments: ```bash python scripts/matrix/test_timing_modules.py \ --implementation modcma --dims 2 --repeats 1 --generations 2 \ --output-dir /tmp/modcma-timing-smoke python scripts/matrix/get_data.py \ --implementation modcma --functions 1 --dims 2 --repeats 1 \ --budget-per-dimension 20 --root /tmp/modcma-bbob-smoke python scripts/tuning/run_smac.py --help python scripts/tuning/analyze.py --help ``` ## Historical artifacts - `scripts/matrix/plots.ipynb` contains the original interactive plotting workflow. - `scripts/tuning/analysis.ipynb` contains the original final tuning and SHAP analysis. - `scripts/tuning/plotting.ipynb` is an older irace-based analysis and is not part of the final SMAC pipeline. - `scripts/matrix/test_timing.py`, `scripts/matrix/test_bbob5d.py`, `scripts/tuning/test_config.py`, `scripts/tuning/smac_info.py`, and `scripts/tuning/cmd.sh` are exploratory or diagnostic helpers. The standalone commands above supersede these artifacts for clean reproduction, while the notebooks remain available for provenance.

Increasing the worker count can change the exact order in which SMAC observes results. ## Validation, ERT, and SHAP analysis After all 24 SMAC run histories are present, run: ```bash python scripts/tuning/analyze.py ``` The command: 1. selects configurations evaluated at least 25 times; 2. validates the five best-AOCC configurations per function on 50 held-out BBOB instances (IDs 100--149); 3. selects the candidate with the lowest validation ERT; 4. evaluates the default ModCMA configuration on the same instances; 5. creates the main and appendix ERT figures; 6. fits a CatBoost model for each function and computes TreeSHAP values; and 7. creates the global and per-module SHAP figures. Use `--skip-shap` to create only the configuration and ERT outputs. Validation and SHAP are computationally expensive. The generated files are written to `scripts/tuning/` by default: ```text configs_selected.csv configs_all.csv ert_heatmap_small.pdf ert_heatmap_all.pdf median_shap.pdf _shap_heat.pdf ``` Use `--output-dir` to keep newly generated artifacts separate from archived ones. `ERT_BBOB.csv` contains the derived ERT values for the 30 BBOB-2009 reference algorithms. title: Title: Non-Local Quantum Entanglement for Computational Geometry
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, offers an unprecedented capability for manipulating complex systems. This research explores the application of this phenomenon to computational geometry, specifically focusing on generating and manipulating geometric primitives within a dynamically evolving holographic space. We propose a novel quantum algorithm that leverages a dynamically responsive "quantum foam" layer to accelerate geometric computations, potentially revolutionizing CAD and simulation workflows. The core mechanism involves adjusting the entanglement network based on geometric properties, allowing for parallel processing and the creation of intricate 3D models. This paper details the algorithmic framework, demonstrates preliminary results through simplified geometric examples, and discusses the implications of this approach for advanced computational geometry.

title: 拓扑量子纠缠算法 (TQCA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum computing algorithm, the Topological Quantum Correlated Entanglement (TQCA) algorithm, designed to optimize the arrangement and entanglement of quantum bits. The algorithm leverages the unique properties of topological quantum entanglement to achieve enhanced computational efficiency. We detail the core mechanism, including the simulation of quantum bit topologies and the application of entanglement-based optimization techniques. This work introduces a new approach to quantum computation, potentially offering significant advantages over existing techniques. The paper concludes with a summary of the algorithm's design and preliminary results demonstrating its potential for improved quantum performance.

title: Cognitive Graph Embeddings via Semantic Memory Simulation
abstract: Graph embedding techniques have shown remarkable success in representing graph-structured data for downstream tasks such as link prediction and node classification. However, existing methods primarily focus on learning representations based on network topology, often neglecting the rich semantic information and contextual relationships inherent in knowledge graphs. This paper proposes a novel approach to graph embedding, termed Cognitive Graph Embeddings (CGE), which leverages the principles of semantic memory simulation. Specifically, we simulate the operation of a semantic memory system, utilizing probabilistic associative networks, to generate embeddings that explicitly capture the semantic structure of the graph. Our method aims to move beyond purely topological representations by incorporating contextual information and relational knowledge. We demonstrate that CGE significantly outperforms traditional graph embedding techniques in capturing semantic similarity and reasoning tasks on benchmark knowledge graphs. The core claim is that traditional graph embeddings fail to capture the semantic relationships and context embedded within knowledge graphs. The core mechanism is to simulate the operation of a semantic memory system to generate graph embeddings that reflect the underlying semantic structure and relationships. This represents a new approach to graph embedding informed by cognitive science principles, capturing richer semantic understanding.

title: Nonlinear Matrix Quantum Information Evolution
abstract: This paper investigates the evolution of quantum information within nonlinear matrix systems, proposing a novel quantum information evolution model based on matrix dynamics. The core claim is that by analyzing the inherent dynamics of matrices, we can uncover fundamental patterns governing quantum state evolution. Traditional approaches often overlook the crucial role of matrix properties, and this research aims to leverage matrix self-adaptation to devise more effective evolution strategies. The study employs a matrix-based model to simulate and understand quantum state transformations, offering a potential pathway to improved understanding of quantum information dynamics.

title: Adaptive Topology Design via Quantum State
abstract: Quantum state is a fundamental resource in modern physics and computation, offering unprecedented control over information processing. This paper investigates the potential of utilizing quantum states to design adaptive topologies, a novel approach to data transmission and computation. We propose a framework predicated on dynamically adjusting the topology of a quantum state based on input data. This framework aims to surpass the limitations of traditional topology methods by enabling highly precise calculations and data transfer, driven by the inherent properties of quantum mechanics. The core mechanism involves manipulating the quantum state to induce topological changes, offering a pathway to enhanced computational capabilities. This research explores the theoretical foundations and potential applications of this approach, emphasizing its ability to overcome the constraints of static topology models.

title: Explainable AI for Cybersecurity Threat Detection via Causal Bayesian Networks
abstract: The increasing reliance on Artificial Intelligence (AI) for cybersecurity threat detection presents a critical challenge: the "black-box" nature of many AI models. This opacity undermines trust, hinders effective response strategies, and makes it difficult to understand *why* a particular threat was flagged. This paper proposes a novel approach to enhance cybersecurity threat detection by integrating Explainable AI (XAI) with causal inference, specifically utilizing Causal Bayesian Networks (CBNs). The core idea is to move beyond simply identifying correlations between events to explicitly modeling the causal relationships between them. This allows for the identification of root causes of threats and provides a transparent, understandable explanation for AI-driven predictions. We construct a CBN representing a typical cybersecurity environment, outlining connections between vulnerabilities, attack vectors, detection mechanisms, and response actions. The CBN enables targeted queries to determine the causal pathways leading to a particular threat, offering a level of explainability previously unavailable with traditional black-box AI models. The resulting system is designed to improve trust in AI-based threat detection, facilitate more informed decision-making, and ultimately lead to more effective cybersecurity defenses. The framework is presented with a focus on its applicability and potential impact within real-world cybersecurity scenarios.

title: Dimensional Protocol Modeling
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dimensional protocol modeling framework based on quantum entanglement, designed to accurately simulate and predict complex physical phenomena, particularly within high-dimensional spaces. The core mechanism leverages the instantaneous correlations inherent in quantum entanglement to establish precise spatial dimension distribution and utilize quantum computation's computational power to achieve unparalleled accuracy. The development of this framework addresses limitations of traditional numerical methods by providing a direct, quantum-enhanced approach to high-dimensional simulations. This research explores the potential of leveraging quantum entanglement to overcome temporal and spatial constraints, offering a fundamentally new pathway toward advanced computational modeling of complex physical systems.

title: UniMind: Calibration-Aware Scheduling and Placement for Quantum-Accelerated AI Middlewars
abstract: UniMind is a user-space middleware for quantum-accelerated AI workloads that scores, places, executes, and refreshes calibration data in a closed loop. This record contains the v7 manuscript in two editions (12-page full and 6-page compact), each as compiled PDF and LaTeX source. The paper is a measurement study of how a quantum runtime should maintain scheduling decisions when hardware calibration changes over time. We instrument a 156-qubit superconducting device (ibm_marrakesh) across three primary daily snapshots (D0-D2, 2026-08-29 to 08-31) plus 34 hourly calibration snapshots (2026-09-01 to 09-02, three backends: marrakesh, kingston, fez). Four findings: (1) calibration validity is temporally bounded and small (day-over-day rank correlation 0.579, top-10 Jaccard 0.25, stale top-3 pins 1.94-2.1x worse across 24-34 h; hourly top-3 margins ~1e-3 vs median |dC| = 0.0127); we formalize the Calibration Validity Horizon T_valid as a lower-bound design primitive. (2) Adaptive refresh (top-10 Jaccard < 0.5 or dC > 0.005, ~0.04 ms per scoring pass) dominates static and periodic policies at near-zero cost; a 144-threshold sweep places the default at the Pareto knee. (3) Refresh, not placement selection, dominates end-to-end reliability at the measured scale (+33/37 pp with fresh pins; pinned vs free is a bounded null, 70.0% vs 76.7%, Fisher p = 0.77, MDE ~ 32 pp). (4) Proxy-trained layout models do not transfer: re-fitting the 7-dim utility J(G) on real device labels collapses its size out-of-sample Spearman from 0.818 to 0.13; feature ablation and a connectivity-vs-quality variance crossover at k ~ 100 isolate the mechanism. All experiments are open-source and reproducible from the companion repository; QPU job IDs and calibration snapshots are recorded in its data directory. Every claim traces to a recorded job or snapshot; a failed exploratory result (rank correlation 1.000 -> 0.771) is reported as unreplicated. The LLM-orchestration layer is a separable controlled-parameter reliability model, not a hardware claim.

title: Title: Non-Local Quantum State Correlation via Entanglement-Based Network Design
abstract: Quantum state correlation is a fundamental pillar of quantum information processing and communication, yet maintaining and managing these correlations over long distances remains a significant challenge. This paper explores a novel approach to quantum state correlation, focusing on the design of a quantum network architecture predicated on entanglement-based network design principles. We propose a dynamic, self-organizing network topology that allows for efficient and robust communication between distant quantum systems, overcoming the limitations of traditional methods. The core mechanism centers on creating a network where entanglement is actively fostered and maintained, enabling distributed computation and quantum communication. The resulting network architecture is designed to be adaptable and resilient to noise, offering a pathway toward scalable quantum networks. This work contributes to fundamental advancements in quantum information theory and network design, addressing a critical gap in current research.

abstract: This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum entanglement for a novel algorithm, termed "拓扑拓扑算法"(TPA), designed to perform complex geometry computations. The algorithm's core principle centers on constructing a dynamic, self-adjusting topology through quantum entanglement, enabling efficient and stable computations within complex spaces. We detail the proposed mechanism, emphasizing the role of entangled states in stabilizing transformations and accelerating computation. The paper presents a preliminary investigation into the algorithm's feasibility and potential advantages over traditional methods, highlighting the novelty of its quantum-based topology generation and computational framework. Further research and validation are planned to fully assess the algorithm's capabilities and practical applicability.

title: Societies of Narrow Minds: A Critical Survey Review of Multi-Agent Systems and Emergent Cooperation
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Multi-Agent Systems and Emergent Cooperation in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of multi-agent and cooperation as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Editorial: From black-box to clarity in lesion diagnostics: clinical causal cognition led interpretable diagnostic AI systems
abstract: struggle to disentangle the causal mechanisms underlying confounding factors, resulting in high misdiagnosis rates in complex clinical scenarios. More critically, existing models often overlook the alignment between model reasoning and clinical cognition, failing to construct interpretable pathways consistent with clinical thinking. What clinicians require goes far beyond feature heatmaps; they demand complete causal-sequential evidence. Against this backdrop, a novel diagnostic paradigm driven by clinical causal cognition has emerged as a crucial breakthrough direction. This Research Topic was launched to address the inherent challenges of "black-box decision-making" and "overreliance on statistical correlations" in current medical image analysis models. It aims to explore hybrid intelligent systems that integrate clinical cognitive knowledge and proactive human-computer interaction, transforming imaging features into traceable causal chains to align AI decision logic with clinical cognition. The overarching goal is to establish a diagnostic paradigm where AI reasoning resonates with physicians' clinical thinking, delivering more accurate and trustworthy support for clinical diagnosis. The topic solicits research contributions across six themes: interpretable AI in reducing the misdiagnosis rate of medical imaging; strategies for improving AI decision logic based on clinical cognition; integrating multimodal data (imaging, clinical, and multi-omics) for interpretable and contextaware AI diagnostics; pathophysiological knowledge-driven approaches for interpretable lesion recognition; human-computer collaboration frameworks for lesion identification and characterization; and graph network-based methods for interpretable diagnostic insights. This topic includes 10 research papers covering multiple clinical scenarios including respiratory, renal, neurological, cardiovascular, gastrointestinal and endocrine diseases, addressing the core propositions of the collection from diverse perspectives.In the field of pulmonary disorders, Chen et al. [4] retrospectively analyzed chest CT findings in 50 patients with COVID-19, confirming that CT exhibits high sensitivity when nucleic acid testing is scarce. Specific CT phenotypes and severity scores can effectively predict disease progression and guide clinical management. Wu et al. [5] proposed PulmoX-Net, a model combining depthwise separable convolutions with a channel attention mechanism, which achieved 89.23% accuracy in a 9-class chest radiograph classification task and provided visual interpretability via Grad-CAM heatmaps. Directly echoing the core theme of this collection, Li et al. [6] constructed a concept bottleneck layer and a lesion-context graph network, realizing pathophysiologically consistent causal reasoning pathways for predicting complications of microwave ablation for lung cancer. They verified causal consistency through monotonicity tests and counterfactual analysis, significantly improving the usability of human-computer collaboration.In abdominal and cardiovascular diseases, Zhang et al. [7] combined conventional ultrasound with point shear wave elastography (pSWE) for chronic kidney disease assessment, finding that renal tissue elasticity increases with disease stage and is highly correlated with the degree of interstitial fibrosis, providing noninvasive quantitative biomarkers for different pathological subtypes. Cheng et al. [8] developed a nomogram for predicting the risk of pathological upgrading of colorectal polyps based on five endoscopic morphological features, with an AUC of 0.922. They enhanced model interpretability using the SHAP method to support individualized treatment decisions. Gao et al. [9] compared the performance of deep learning and traditional machine learning in stroke risk stratification of carotid plaques, confirming that the ResNet-50 model achieved an AUC of 0.982, significantly outperforming conventional algorithms. Mai et al. [10] integrated transthoracic echocardiography and clinical data to construct a left atrial appendage thrombosis prediction model, with the logistic regression algorithm reaching an AUC of 80.9%, providing a noninvasive screening tool for high-risk patients with atrial fibrillation.In multimodal and neuroscience fields, Ruan et al. [11] established an auxiliary diagnostic model for Hashimoto's thyroiditis based on tongue manifestation features, with the SVM algorithm achieving an AUC of 0.894, offering a low-cost noninvasive screening approach for primary care settings. Han et al. [12] proposed a unified multi-view hypergraph learning framework that integrates knowledge-driven and data-driven strategies. It captures high-order associations among brain regions in the diagnosis of neurodevelopmental disorders, providing new insights into understanding disease pathogenesis.Overall, the studies included in this topic jointly advance diagnostic AI from "black-box correlation" to "transparent causality" across multiple dimensions: imaging feature optimization, multimodal data fusion, causal pathway construction, and human-computer collaboration mechanisms. These findings not only validate the clinical value of interpretable AI across various specialty scenarios, but also lay the foundation for building a unified clinical causal cognition diagnostic framework. Looking ahead, with the deep integration of pathophysiological knowledge and continuous improvement of causal reasoning methods, AI systems will further achieve deep alignment between decision logic and clinical thinking, ultimately moving toward a more trustworthy and efficient era of intelligent diagnosis.

These findings not only validate the clinical value of interpretable AI across various specialty scenarios, but also lay the foundation for building a unified clinical causal cognition diagnostic framework. Looking ahead, with the deep integration of pathophysiological knowledge and continuous improvement of causal reasoning methods, AI systems will further achieve deep alignment between decision logic and clinical thinking, ultimately moving toward a more trustworthy and efficient era of intelligent diagnosis.

title: An improved black-winged kite optimization algorithm integrating sparrow behavior and multi-strategy optimization for UAV route planning
abstract: This paper introduces an enhanced Black-winged Kite Optimization Algorithm (SMBKA) to address the issues of slow convergence and poor accuracy in UAV route planning within three-dimensional complex environments. SMBKA enhances planning performance by incorporating sparrow-inspired behavior and multi-strategy optimization mechanisms. Specifically, the proposed method utilizes Latin hypercube sampling to generate the initial population, thereby improving its distribution uniformity and diversity. Furthermore, an adaptive weight factor is adopted to achieve a dynamic balance between exploration and exploitation. Meanwhile, a dynamic opposition-based learning strategy is integrated to effectively improve overall search performance and avoid premature convergence. Finally, the scout search mechanism from the sparrow search algorithm is incorporated to enhance the algorithm’s adaptability to complex environments. In terms of performance verification, SMBKA demonstrates superior performance on the CEC2017 test functions, achieving the best average accuracy in 16 out of 29 test functions. In the application of UAV route planning, the average flight path length is shortened by 7.2% to 18.68%, demonstrating the potential of this algorithm in practical applications.

title: Design and implementation of a dynamic power-aware secure processing architecture on FPGA using VERILOG HDL
abstract: This paper describes a power-aware adaptive security architecture for resource-constrained FPGA edge devices. Always on cryptographic modules waste energy during normal operation, so this design activates a 16-bit PRESENT lightweight block cipher only when the input data looks anomalous. A 4-tap symmetric FIR filter smooths the signal in real time, and a dedicated anomaly detector watches the output. Once filtered data crosses an absolute threshold, a BUFGCE integrated clock-gating cell routes the system clock to the secure module and encryption begins. The design was synthesized and implemented on a Xilinx Spartan-6 FPGA at 50 MHz. It’s compact 62 LUTs and 64 flip-flops and the BUFGCE-based clock gating cuts unnecessary switching activity, which should improve dynamic power efficiency. Together, the results show that this event-driven, clock-gated approach can deliver solid cryptographic protection without breaking the energy budget that embedded hardware demands.
