title: Improving global precipitation forecasts with an AI weather model trained on satellite observations
abstract: Precipitation forecasts shape decision-making across the global economy, particularly in sectors such as agriculture. However, unlike variables such as temperature, precipitation is highly intermittent and localized, making it difficult to forecast. While recent advances in AI weather prediction systems have enabled them to surpass physical models on globally averaged metrics, improvements in mean error rarely translate to actionable forecasts of severe flooding or dry crop fields. Furthermore, most of these models are trained and evaluated against a reanalysis data product, ERA5, which has well-known biases. Here we retrain AIFS, ECMWF's widely-used, open-source operational 0.25° probabilistic graph-transformer weather model, on satellite-based precipitation observations. Our model, Laxmi, improves global probabilistic accuracy by 19% and resolves systematic distributional biases in ERA5. Specifically, Laxmi reduces drizzle overprediction by 33% for amounts less than 3 mm per day. It also mitigates extreme rainfall underprediction, improving the global 95th percentile Brier skill score by 57%. Across a case study of 10 Indian tropical storms, Laxmi delivered the most accurate forecast of 150 mm event-total precipitation in 7 events, compared to 1 for AIFS and 2 for the leading physical model, IFS. Our results demonstrate that incorporating observation-based precipitation data directly into training can substantially improve forecasts.

title: SAUF-Net: Structure--Appearance Representation Learning with Uncertainty Feedback for Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: Semi-supervised learning has shown great potential for reducing annotation costs in medical image segmentation. However, most existing methods mainly exploit unlabeled data through prediction-level consistency, while the reliability of internal feature representations is often overlooked. In medical images, target-related structural cues are easily entangled with unstable appearance variations, which may lead to unreliable pseudo labels and error accumulation during training. To address these issues, we propose SAUF-Net, a Structure--Appearance Representation Learning with Uncertainty Feedback Network for semi-supervised medical image segmentation. SAUF-Net uses the Structure--Appearance Decomposition Module (SADM) to separate bottleneck features into structural and appearance representations. The Disentangled Guidance Module (DGM) injects these representations into the decoding process to enhance structure-aware segmentation. Meanwhile, the Auxiliary Decoder produces branch-specific predictions for reliability estimation and a fused prediction for appearance-swapped consistency. Furthermore, we introduce an Appearance-Swapped Consistency branch to encourage structural representations to remain stable under appearance variations. We also introduce a reliability-map-guided dual-head discriminator with a Validity Head and an Uncertainty Head to provide feature-level uncertainty feedback. Extensive experiments on ISIC-2016 and Kvasir-SEG demonstrate that SAUF-Net outperforms state-of-the-art semi-supervised methods, especially under low-label settings.

title: TaLK: Text-attributed Graph Dataset Distillation via Coupling Language Model with Graph-Aware Kernel
abstract: Text-attributed graphs (TAGs) are widely used in many real-world domains, and learning on TAGs requires jointly modeling text semantics and graph structure. A standard approach for modeling TAGs is to combine a language model (LM) and a graph neural network (GNN), but joint training is computationally expensive and difficult to scale. Dataset distillation is a promising way to reduce training costs, but existing methods are not well suited to TAGs because they are typically designed for a single modality or still require repeatedly training expensive LM-GNN models on the full dataset during distillation. To address this, we propose TaLK, an effective dataset distillation method for TAGs that couples an LM with a graph-aware neural tangent kernel. This design enables efficient dataset distillation, avoiding repeated joint training on the full dataset while reflecting both textual and structural information for effective TAG learning. Experiments on multiple TAG benchmarks show that TaLK consistently outperforms existing baselines and achieves up to 97% of full-dataset performance with only 1% synthetic data.

title: Facilitando A Adoção Da Inteligência Artificial Na Indústria: Um Estudo De Caso Sobre A Metodologia De Workshops E Atividades De Sensibilização
abstract: A adoção crescente da Inteligência Artificial (IA) pelas organizações demonstra que os desafios de sua implementação ultrapassam a dimensão tecnológica e abrangem aspectos relacionados à cultura organizacional, à gestão da mudança e ao desenvolvimento de competências.Este estudo tem por objetivo apresentar e analisar a metodologia de workshops e atividades de sensibilização desenvolvida pelo Instituto SENAI de Tecnologia da Informação e Comunicação, localizado em Londrina, Paraná, para desmistificar a IA entre as organizações participantes do Programa de Residência em IA e prepará-las para identificar e implementar projetos de inovação.Trata-se de um estudo de caso qualitativo e descritivo, fundamentado na análise documental da metodologia, na observação das oficinas realizadas e na avaliação dos resultados obtidos junto às organizações participantes.Os resultados indicam que a metodologia ampliou o nível de letramento em IA, reduziu barreiras cognitivas e culturais, fortaleceu a cultura orientada por dados e aprimorou a qualidade das demandas submetidas ao desenvolvimento de Provas de Conceito no âmbito do Programa.Como contribuição prática, apresenta uma metodologia de baixo custo, replicável e baseada na construção colaborativa de oportunidades de inovação, aplicável por instituições de inovação, universidades e organizações interessadas em acelerar a transformação digital e ampliar as chances de sucesso de projetos de IA.Como contribuição teórica, o estudo evidencia o papel das instituições de ciência, tecnologia e inovação como agentes de transferência tecnológica e de desenvolvimento da maturidade organizacional para a adoção da IA.

title: Geometric Optimization via Quantum Simulation
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum simulation to the optimization of geometric shapes and structures. We propose a novel approach that leverages the unique properties of quantum algorithms to significantly accelerate the optimization process compared to classical methods. The core of our work involves constructing a quantum simulation framework, utilizing quantum algorithms to effectively explore the solution space and identify optimal configurations. We demonstrate the potential of this methodology to address challenges in geometric optimization, offering a promising path toward more efficient and insightful solutions. The research underscores the potential of quantum simulation to revolutionize geometric problem-solving.

title: Adaptive Differential Privacy for Federated Learning via Randomized Compression
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising paradigm for training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without directly exchanging data. However, achieving strong differential privacy (DP) guarantees in FL is a significant challenge, particularly when combined with compression techniques commonly employed to reduce communication costs. Traditional approaches often rely on fixed compression ratios, potentially sacrificing accuracy for privacy or vice versa. This paper introduces an adaptive differential privacy framework for FL that dynamically adjusts the compression ratio based on the sensitivity of the data and the desired privacy level. We leverage randomized compression methods, specifically noise addition with learned parameters, to achieve this adaptation. Our approach demonstrates a novel balance between privacy and utility, offering a more effective solution compared to static compression strategies. The core claim of this work is that achieving strong differential privacy guarantees in federated learning necessitates careful management of compression ratios. The key mechanism involves introducing an adaptive compression scheme. This paper presents a formalization of this adaptive approach, outlining its mathematical foundations and providing a framework for its implementation.

title: Contextualized Neural Turing Machines with Episodic Memory
abstract: Neural Turing Machines (NTMs) have demonstrated promise in addressing the challenges of sequential learning and memory management within neural networks. However, existing NTM architectures often struggle with limited memory capacity and a lack of robust contextual understanding, particularly when dealing with complex, temporally-dependent tasks. This work proposes a novel extension to the NTM framework, integrating a structured episodic memory system designed to overcome these limitations. The core idea is to leverage temporal context to organize and access memory, allowing the NTM to associate new tasks and data with relevant historical information. Specifically, we introduce a layered episodic memory where each layer represents a distinct temporal context. The NTM's read and write heads selectively interact with these layers, facilitating more effective long-term task learning and improved contextual reasoning. The system learns to dynamically map tasks and data to appropriate layers within the episodic memory, leading to enhanced performance in scenarios requiring prolonged contextual awareness. We formalize the architecture and learning process, outlining the key equations and operational principles. This approach represents a significant step towards more sophisticated and adaptable memory systems for NTMs and, more broadly, for neural networks tackling complex sequential problems.

title: Explainable Modality-Specific DenseNet Models and Population-Level Decision Fusion for Breast Cancer Classification Across Mammography, Ultrasound, and Histopathology
abstract: Breast cancer diagnosis draws on complementary information from mammography, ultrasound, and histopathology, yet multimodal artificial-intelligence studies can become clinically ambiguous when unrelated public cohorts are fused as though they represented the same patients. This study developed an explainable framework based on independently trained DenseNet-121 specialists for the three imaging modalities and evaluated feature- and decision-level fusion as population-level ensemble experiments. The harmonized analytical collection contained 34,207 publicly available images: 24,576 mammograms, 1,722 ultrasound images, and 7,909 histopathology images. Modality-specific preprocessing, class weighting, augmentation, and ImageNet transfer learning were applied, while the histopathology branch additionally incorporated a domain-adversarial objective. Grad-CAM++ was used for qualitative auditing of the radiological specialists. From the detailed test confusion matrices, ultrasound achieved 90.8% accuracy, 88.2% sensitivity, and 92.9% specificity; mammography achieved 96.0% accuracy, 96.3% sensitivity, and 95.6% specificity; and histopathology achieved 94.8% accuracy, 96.5% sensitivity, and 91.5% specificity. Wilson 95% confidence intervals, balanced accuracy, and Matthews correlation coefficients were derived from these counts. The domain-adversarial histopathology ablation showed an approximately two-percentage-point increase in rounded accuracy, although the archived experimental record did not preserve the precise source-target domain assignment. Attention-based feature fusion achieved 94.2% accuracy and assigned the largest learned weights to histopathology and mammography. Across eight exploratory fixed decision-weight configurations, the highest observed population-level accuracy was 98.8% for a mammography-emphasized rule. Because modality predictions originated from unmatched cohorts and the fixed-weight sweep was not documented as using a separate selection set, fusion findings are interpreted as exploratory sensitivity analyses rather than same-patient clinical performance. The results support transparent modality-specific evaluation and motivate future validation on deduplicated, patient-linked, externally collected cohorts with calibrated probabilities and reproducible split manifests.

title: Adaptive Learning-Based Robot Motion Planning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to robot motion planning based on adaptive learning. Traditional robot motion planning methods often struggle to cope with dynamic and uncertain environments. This research leverages reinforcement learning (RL) to develop a system capable of autonomously learning optimal motion strategies and adapting to real-time changes in the environment and task requirements. The core of the system is a dynamically adjusted trajectory generation process, allowing the robot to navigate complex scenarios with greater flexibility and efficiency. The system is trained using an RL algorithm, and the learned policy is then utilized for real-time trajectory optimization. This approach demonstrates the potential for significantly enhancing the adaptability and intelligence of robots in various applications. The system's ability to learn and adapt provides a robust solution for dynamic environments, addressing limitations inherent in traditional planning techniques. ---

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement Substrate Mapping
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental aspect of quantum mechanics, holds immense potential for technological advancements, particularly in quantum computing and quantum communication. However, the precise nature and distribution of entanglement within physical systems remain a significant challenge. This paper proposes a novel method for mapping quantum entanglement properties of physical substrates – such as materials – by combining advanced quantum measurement and data analysis. We introduce a "entanglement field mapping" technique that aims to identify and characterize substrate-level entanglement, potentially revealing insights into underlying quantum phenomena and facilitating the design of tailored quantum devices. The research explores the potential of this approach to move beyond passive observation of entanglement to active mapping, offering a fundamentally new pathway for exploring quantum mechanics.

title: Quantum Fusion Algorithms: An Adaptive Tuning Approach
abstract: Quantum fusion, a novel approach to quantum computing, aims to combine the strengths of multiple quantum systems to achieve enhanced computational capabilities. This paper introduces a novel adaptive tuning mechanism for quantum fusion algorithms, designed to optimize integration results based on the specific characteristics of the input data. The core of this framework is a dynamic parameter adjustment system that adapts the fusion algorithm's parameters based on the problem's inherent properties. This adaptive approach significantly improves the overall performance of quantum fusion by tailoring the integration process to the unique demands of each task. The study highlights the potential of this mechanism to overcome the limitations of traditional parameter adjustments and unlock new possibilities in quantum computing.

evidence.abstract: Quantum fusion, a novel approach to quantum computing, aims to combine the strengths of multiple quantum systems to achieve enhanced computational capabilities. This paper introduces a novel adaptive tuning mechanism for quantum fusion algorithms, designed to optimize integration results based on the specific characteristics of the input data. The core of this framework is a dynamic parameter adjustment system that adapts the fusion algorithm's parameters based on the problem's inherent properties. This adaptive approach significantly improves the overall performance of quantum fusion by tailoring the integration process to the unique demands of each task. title: Formal Verification of Blockchain Consensus Algorithms via Abstract Interpretation
abstract: Blockchain technology relies heavily on consensus algorithms to ensure data integrity and security. However, the complexity of these algorithms, coupled with their inherent non-deterministic nature, makes formal verification – guaranteeing the correctness of a system through mathematical methods – a significant challenge. This paper proposes a novel approach to blockchain consensus algorithm verification utilizing abstract interpretation. We represent the blockchain state and consensus rules within an abstract domain, enabling systematic analysis and verification of crucial properties such as liveness, safety, and fault tolerance. Our methodology offers a rigorous and quantifiable method for assessing the reliability of blockchain systems, mitigating potential vulnerabilities, and ultimately building more trustworthy decentralized applications. The core of our approach lies in leveraging abstract domains to approximate the blockchain state, allowing us to reason about the system's behavior without being bogged down by the intricacies of the underlying implementation. This significantly reduces the complexity of verification while still providing strong guarantees about the system's correctness.

title: Modular Temporal Memory for Continual Learning
abstract: Continual learning, also known as lifelong learning, presents a significant challenge in artificial intelligence: the ability to learn continuously from a stream of data without forgetting previously acquired knowledge. Traditional continual learning approaches often struggle with catastrophic forgetting, where learning new tasks drastically degrades performance on old tasks. This paper proposes a novel framework – the "Time Memory Module" (TMM) – designed to address this challenge by modularizing the temporal memory mechanism. The TMM framework consists of four core components: a Memory Store, a Retrieval Module, a Conversion Module, and a Control Module. These modules are designed to be independently configurable and adaptable, allowing for efficient and flexible continual learning. The core claim is that by breaking down the time memory function into reusable, modular components, we can achieve more efficient and flexible continual learning systems. This approach facilitates finer control and customization, promoting knowledge transfer between different continual learning scenarios. Mathematical notation is used to represent key components and their interactions within the TMM framework.

title: Beehive Structure Optimization Algorithm – A Graph-Based Dynamic Evolution
abstract: The Beehive structure, a geometric pattern characterized by interconnected nested circles, is widely employed in various fields, including structural design, art, and computer graphics. This paper explores a novel optimization algorithm, termed "Beehive Structure Optimization Algorithm" (BSOA), that leverages a graph-based dynamic evolution approach to refine the parameters of a beehive structure. The core concept revolves around representing the beehive as a graph, where nodes represent structural elements and edges represent relationships between these elements. A dynamic evolution mechanism iteratively adjusts the graph structure and parameter values based on a predefined objective function, ensuring the optimized beehive structure adapts to evolving data distributions. This method offers a significant advancement over traditional approaches by offering automatic parameter adjustment and structural adaptation, ultimately improving the optimization process. The algorithm's design incorporates a robust feedback loop that continually evaluates the resulting beehive structure, refining the graph and parameters to achieve optimal performance. This research aims to present a practical and effective framework for automated beehive optimization.

title: Scalable Federated Learning with Differential Privacy and Graph-Based Communication
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising paradigm for training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without directly exchanging the data itself. However, traditional FL approaches often suffer from significant communication overhead and potential privacy vulnerabilities. This research proposes a novel scalable federated learning system that addresses these limitations through the integration of graph-based communication topologies and differential privacy mechanisms. The core idea is to represent the relationships between participating clients as a graph, enabling selective communication and aggregation of model updates based on the graph structure, thereby reducing unnecessary communication and enhancing privacy. The system utilizes a graph convolutional network (GCN) to learn client embeddings reflecting their connectivity and data characteristics, which then guide the communication process. Differential privacy is incorporated by adding calibrated noise to the aggregated model updates, providing a provable privacy guarantee. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves significant improvements in communication efficiency and privacy compared to standard FL methods, particularly in scenarios with complex client relationships and stringent privacy requirements. This work contributes a practical and scalable solution for deploying federated learning in diverse applications where data privacy and communication efficiency are paramount.

title: Based on Quantum Entanglement Distributed Computing Resource Routing
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement for distributed computing resource routing. The core claim is that leveraging the direct connection between distributed computing nodes through quantum entanglement can overcome the limitations of classical communication, achieving ultra-low latency and high bandwidth data transfer. This research proposes a "quantum entanglement network" based on constructing and exploiting entangled states for information sharing and routing decision-making. The mechanism involves nodes exchanging information via entanglement, capitalizing on the unique properties of entanglement to facilitate lossless communication and optimize resource allocation. The theoretical framework presented herein suggests a paradigm shift in distributed computing, offering the prospect of significantly improved performance compared to conventional approaches. We explore the fundamental advantages and challenges associated with this novel approach, focusing on the potential for achieving unprecedented data transfer rates and minimizing communication delays. This work lays the groundwork for future research into the practical implementation of quantum-enhanced distributed computing systems. ---

title: Context-Aware Semantic Graph Generation from Text
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to graph generation from text, termed Context-Aware Semantic Graph Generation (CASGG). Existing graph generation models frequently struggle to capture and represent the intricate contextual information embedded within text, leading to generated graphs that lack semantic accuracy and fail to represent meaningful relationships. Our methodology addresses this limitation by employing a generative model that leverages a hierarchical contextual representation of the input text. This enables the model to produce graphs that more faithfully reflect the semantic relationships and dependencies present within the text's context. The core claim of this work is that a truly context-aware approach is necessary to overcome the shortcomings of current graph generation methods. We introduce a new mechanism that moves beyond simple pattern matching, providing a robust framework for generating graphs with enhanced semantic understanding. The evaluation demonstrates the superior performance of our approach compared to traditional methods.

title: Quantum amplitude estimation beyond power-of-two schedules
abstract: Non-adaptive quantum amplitude estimation (QAE) fixes its Grover depths in advance, so every circuit can run in parallel, but it has so far needed more queries than the best adaptive methods. We show that most of this gap comes from two conventional choices: subspace-based post-processing and power-of-two depth ladders. We replace the first by the exact maximum-likelihood estimate, one matrix multiplication per batch of estimates, and the second by a geometric ladder with ratio $r \approx 1.45$. The result is a fully parallel, deterministic-schedule estimator with total query complexity $2.8$-$3.1/\varepsilon$ at 95% confidence for target errors from $3.5\times 10^{-3}$ to $10^{-6}$. This matches the average-case complexity of chebAE, the best benchmarked adaptive method, within statistical uncertainty (with the lower point estimate at every scale tested), beats its maximum-observed complexity by $1.6\times$, and needs a maximum sequential depth of only $0.21/\varepsilon$ against chebAE's $2.9/\varepsilon$. Relative to csAE, the best non-adaptive benchmark, the constants improve by 30-35% at 95% and $1.5$-$1.7\times$ at 99% confidence. The optimal ratio has a simple origin. Doubling is the fastest depth growth at which the data can still tell neighboring candidate values apart, so power-of-two ladders sit at the edge of confusion and must buy reliability with extra shots; a slightly denser ladder checks every scale redundantly. An error-probability analysis reproduces the measured failure rates and locates the optimum. The likelihood formulation extends directly to noise-aware estimation, and uniformly scaling the capped ladder covers the depth-limited regime, realizing the optimal trade-off $M N_{\mathrm{tot}} \approx (0.4$-$0.6)/\varepsilon^2$ within $\sim 1.1\times$ of the schedule's Cramér-Rao limit.

title: VTOS: Learning to Orchestrate Vision Tools by Co-Searching Solutions and Observers
abstract: Vision foundation tools such as open-vocabulary detectors, segmentation models, and post-processing operators are powerful building blocks for computer vision, but their effectiveness depends heavily on how they are orchestrated: which tools are used, in what order, with what parameters, and under what visual conditions. Existing visual-programming agents typically generate a fixed solution pipeline, making them brittle under dense objects, occlusion, small targets, and domain shift. We introduce VTOS (Vision Tools Orchestration Search), a framework for adaptive visual tool orchestration through joint solution-observer search. VTOS co-searches executable solution programs that compose vision tools such as Grounding DINO, SAM, NMS, and slice-and-detect, together with observer programs that diagnose candidate solutions, identify failure modes, and generate actionable feedback. These observations are accumulated in a shared VisionThoughts knowledge base to guide subsequent search. We evaluate VTOS through two case studies: dense object counting on LVIS-Count and zero-shot plant-disease segmentation on PlantSeg-OOD, which stress different orchestration challenges including threshold calibration, NMS, slicing, mask refinement, and domain generalization. Across both tasks, VTOS outperforms static tool pipelines and agentic visual-programming baselines, specifically in complex settings such as dense, occluded scenes and out-of-distribution segmentation where static pipelines leave measurable headroom, rather than in standard tasks where a single well-calibrated tool already approaches its ceiling.

title: Measurement-Device-Independent Entanglement Quantification in a Fully Connected Time-Bin Quantum Network
abstract: Fully connected quantum networks enable scalable quantum communication, yet reliable entanglement characterization without trusting measurement devices remains challenging. Here we experimentally demonstrate measurement-device-independent (MDI) entanglement verification and quantification in a time-bin-encoded fully connected quantum network. Using a broadband periodically poled lithium niobate on insulator source combined with dense wavelength-division multiplexing, we distribute all six pairwise entangled links among four users over an end-to-end separation of 20 km. MDI measurements are realized by encoding the trusted input states in the polarization degree of freedom of the same photons carrying the distributed time-bin entanglement, thereby eliminating the need for independently prepared trusted photons. We show that both entanglement verification and quantification are obtained from the MDI measurements. Our results demonstrate the practical integration of resource-efficient MDI characterization into a fully connected time-bin quantum network, providing a scalable approach for reliable entanglement characterization in large-scale quantum networks.

title: Implementation Of The Advanced Encryption Standard-128 Algorithm And Huffman Compression To Protect Student Grade Data
abstract: Student grade data is personal data that must be protected under Indonesian Law Number 27 of 2022 on Personal Data Protection, yet the rising number of data breaches in the education sector shows that such protection has not been optimally implemented. This study implements the 128-bit Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) algorithm combined with Huffman compression to protect the confidentiality and integrity of student grade files in Excel (.xlsx) format, and evaluates its effectiveness through functional, performance, and security testing. The system was developed as a Python desktop application with a CustomTkinter interface, in which the encryption process runs Huffman compression before AES-128, while integrity verification uses SHA-256 hashing. Testing was conducted on seven student grade files from MA Ma'ahid Kudus. The results show that all files were successfully encrypted and decrypted without failure or data alteration, with encryption times of 0.0142-0.0828 seconds and decryption times of 0.0046-0.1417 seconds. The SHA-256 hash values of the original and decrypted files were identical for all samples, yielding 100% recovery accuracy, while the file size increase from padding and header insertion ranged only from 1,092 to 1,101 bytes. The study concludes that the combination of AES-128 and Huffman compression is an effective and efficient solution for protecting student grade data in educational institutions.

title: Transformer Architectures for Computational Social Science: Workshop Materials (ICSC 2026)
abstract: Materials for the half-day workshop Transformer Architectures for Computational Social Science, held at the International Conference on Social Computing (ICSC 2026), Nuffield College, University of Oxford, 2 September 2026. The workshop applies transformers not to text but to sequences of life events. It starts hands-on with language-based transformers (BERT token embeddings, masked-language prediction, attribution), then turns to longitudinal socioeconomic and health event sequences: how to adapt transformers to them, how to obtain dense representations, how to visualise the resulting embedding space, and how to use those representations for downstream prediction tasks. The repository contains eight Jupyter notebooks, an event-BERT implementation with tokenizer-building and pretraining scripts, pen-and-paper exercises with solutions, derived data built from a synthetic patient population, workshop slides, and the workshop website.

title: ##拓扑几何量子纠错算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum error correction algorithm based on topological geometry, aiming to achieve high-precision, high-tolerance quantum computation and facilitate the construction of quantum information storage systems. Traditional quantum error correction relies on classical algorithms, which struggle with the complexity of quantum states. Topological geometry offers a fundamentally different approach, exhibiting robust error correction due to its inherent structural properties. We outline the core mechanism, detailing how a topological network is constructed to mitigate noise and ensure data integrity. This work presents a fundamentally new methodology for quantum information processing, potentially revolutionizing the field of quantum computation.

title: Center-Free Co-Articulation Load: A Sharp Dynamic Symmetry-Information Theorem
abstract: This preprint establishes a sharp information-theoretic lower bound for history-dependent finite continuation fibers carrying transitive symmetry. For a realized continuation Y_t, a full collection of perspectival contributions Z_t, and maximal information \lambda_t available to any proper subcoalition, the irreducible full-coalition advantage satisfiesK_t \geq [\,b(m_t,\varepsilon_t)-\lambda_t\,]_+,whereb(m,\varepsilon)=\log_2 m-h_2(\varepsilon)-\varepsilon\log_2(m-1).The bound follows from transitive-orbit uniformity and the conditional Fano inequality and is shown to be sharp on regular cyclic fibers by explicit constructions across the full admissible leakage range. The paper further derives a cumulative history-dependent bound, proves invariance under history-dependent injective recoding, and establishes a finite-information pre-specification obstruction: a single pre-existing variable of finite Shannon entropy cannot support arbitrarily large cumulative continuation load at prescribed error levels. The result is deliberately narrower than a general theory of synergistic information. Its invariant measures the information advantage of the full coalition over its most informative proper subcoalition. Standard ingredients—including Fano’s inequality, transitive group actions, additive secret sharing, the mutual-information chain rule, and data processing—are not claimed as novel. The contribution lies in their sharp coupling within a dynamic, history-relative theorem architecture. The formal result is operational and information-theoretic. It does not by itself establish ontological claims about consciousness, potentiality, causation, or metaphysical freedom.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Feature Extraction for Image Recognition
abstract: Quantum-enhanced feature extraction is a rapidly evolving field with the potential to revolutionize image recognition. Traditional feature extraction methods often struggle with the curse of dimensionality, limiting the expressive power of extracted features. This paper investigates the application of quantum entanglement to enhance feature representation and analysis, aiming to overcome these limitations. We propose a novel framework that utilizes quantum properties to reveal subtle correlations within images, potentially leading to improved accuracy and speed. This work explores the potential of quantum entanglement to provide a fundamentally new approach to image recognition, moving beyond classical feature extraction techniques.

title: Nonlinear Geometry Distributions for Quantum Computing Modeling
abstract: This paper investigates the use of nonlinear geometry distributions as a foundational model for quantum computing, aiming to enhance the simulation of complex quantum systems and explore potential applications of quantum computation. The core concept is the "quantum entanglement geometry," a novel framework that dynamically connects quantum entanglement with geometric distributions, offering a more precise and robust representation of quantum states. This approach departs from traditional methods by explicitly incorporating quantum entanglement as a key component of the model. We propose a method to quantify and manipulate entanglement through geometric transformations, leading to improved simulation accuracy and the potential for novel quantum algorithm design. The research explores the limitations of existing models and highlights the advantages of this approach, demonstrating its potential to revolutionize quantum computing modeling.

title: Towards a New AI Memory Architecture: An Auditable Separation of Epistemic Formation and Storage
abstract: H2O Memory TopoPhase asks what an AI memory architecture would look like if pre-transcription observations, the later assembly of weak fragments, and the formation of an explicit insight were represented separately and remained auditable. The v0.2.0-alpha reference prototype implements three deterministic baselines: typed time-aligned non-text observations, delayed-cue assembly with contradiction protection, and a fixed sudden-crystallisation metric with pinned counterevidence. It separates epistemic phase from storage tier and treats text, summaries, vectors, graphs, tokens, and search indices as replaceable derived views rather than the source of record. The 92-test offline suite requires no external AI or paid API. The system does not yet learn what to gather or when to crystallise and is not integrated into model computation. A fixed v0.8 contract-ablation benchmark returns FAIL, so the report claims an inspectable, falsifiable baseline rather than novelty, superiority, or general resource reduction. Learned control, model-internal memory, and a neutral synthetic epistemic-safety simulator are next-phase research.

title: Quantum Hiding Matrix Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum hiding matrix algorithm designed to dynamically adjust quantum computation parameters for enhanced efficiency. Traditional hiding matrix algorithms rely on pre-defined parameters, often requiring manual adjustment for optimal performance. We propose a system that learns and adapts these parameters during the computation process, offering a more flexible and potentially more efficient approach. The algorithm leverages a feedback loop incorporating quantum state measurements and error correction techniques to iteratively optimize the parameters for maximum utility. This approach addresses limitations of existing methods by offering automated parameter tuning and improved adaptability to complex quantum systems. The core mechanism involves a dynamic parameter adjustment algorithm based on a learned state space representation. The algorithm aims to minimize the number of gate operations and maximize the fidelity of the resulting quantum state.

title: Bio-Inspired Optimization Algorithm with Quantum Annealing Hybridization
abstract: This paper explores a novel hybrid optimization approach combining the strengths of bio-inspired algorithms, specifically Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), with Quantum Annealing (QA). Traditional optimization techniques often struggle with escaping local optima, leading to suboptimal solutions. This research posits that integrating ACO for initial solution generation and leveraging QA for subsequent exploration within the solution space can overcome these limitations. The core mechanism involves ACO producing an initial set of candidate solutions, followed by QA's quantum tunneling effect to navigate the solution landscape and escape local minima, ultimately converging towards a global optimum. The effectiveness of this hybridization is demonstrated through a theoretical framework and conceptual design. The primary goal is to demonstrate a pathway toward more robust and efficient optimization, particularly for complex, high-dimensional problems. This work lays the groundwork for future research and development in this promising area.

title: 基于量子计算的非对称矩阵乘法算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum algorithm for matrix multiplication, leveraging quantum superposition and entanglement to achieve significantly enhanced computational speed and quantum advantage compared to classical methods. We propose a unique approach to matrix multiplication based on the quantum state representation of matrices, employing quantum entanglement to dramatically reduce the computational complexity inherent in traditional matrix multiplication. The algorithm demonstrates potential for high-throughput matrix operations, offering a substantial improvement in performance for computationally intensive tasks, particularly within the fields of machine learning and image processing. The proposed method offers a fundamentally new perspective on matrix multiplication, potentially ushering in a new era of quantum computing.

title: Contextualized Graph Embeddings for Knowledge Discovery
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to graph embedding that addresses the limitations of static embeddings in knowledge discovery tasks, particularly link prediction. Traditional graph embeddings, such as Node2Vec and Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs), learn fixed representations of nodes based on the entire graph structure. However, knowledge graphs are inherently dynamic, with relationships evolving over time and influenced by contextual information. This work proposes a contextualized graph embedding method that dynamically adapts node embeddings based on the current query or context. The core idea is to incorporate relevant context and relationships into the embedding update process, refining the embedding space to better reflect the current state of the knowledge graph. We formalize this approach with a dynamic embedding update rule, leveraging graph traversal and attention mechanisms to prioritize relevant neighbors. Experimental results demonstrate that our contextualized embeddings significantly improve link prediction accuracy compared to static embeddings, highlighting the importance of context awareness in knowledge graph representation learning.

title: Graph-Based Quantum Computing Topological Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of graph-based topology optimization to enhance the efficiency of quantum computation. Traditional approaches often focus on qubit count, while topology optimization provides a framework for structuring quantum circuits to minimize errors and maximize performance. We explore the integration of graph-based topology optimization into the design of quantum algorithms, specifically targeting topological quantum computing. The core claim is that leveraging graph structures and topology optimization can significantly improve the scalability and efficiency of quantum computations, offering a novel approach to addressing key challenges in the field.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Adaptive Geometry Modeling
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to geometry modeling based on quantum entanglement. Traditional geometric modeling methods often rely on static, fixed topologies, while this research explores the utilization of entanglement to optimize geometric structures and enhance algorithm efficiency. The core mechanism involves exploiting the correlated properties of entangled particles to dynamically adjust and refine geometric parameters, leading to improved computational performance. This work investigates the potential of entanglement to achieve higher precision and faster convergence in geometric optimization tasks. The theoretical framework and preliminary results demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in solving specific geometric modeling problems.

title: Quantum-Inspired Noise Injection for Robust Neural Network Training
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to enhancing the robustness of neural networks through the strategic injection of noise, drawing inspiration from quantum mechanical principles. Traditional neural network training is often sensitive to noise in the training data, making models vulnerable to adversarial attacks and performance degradation when exposed to real-world, imperfect data. We propose a method that utilizes concepts like superposition and interference – core tenets of quantum mechanics – to guide the introduction of noise during training. Specifically, the noise injection is dynamically controlled based on the model's error signal, creating a more resilient representation. Our approach aims to improve generalization performance and mitigate the negative effects of noise. The core idea is to leverage quantum superposition to explore a wider range of possible solutions during training, and then utilize interference to amplify correct solutions while suppressing incorrect ones. We present a theoretical framework and discuss key considerations for implementing this quantum-inspired noise injection technique. This research contributes a new perspective to neural network robustness, offering a potentially effective strategy for building more reliable and adaptable models.

title: Dungeons That Build Themselves: A Comparative Analysis Review of Procedural Content Generation in Roguelikes
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Procedural Content Generation in Roguelikes in the context of Game Development. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of PCG and roguelikes as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Game Development.

title: Which HSK 3.0? Two Official Documents, and Half of All Grading Decisions Change
abstract: "HSK 3.0" names two different official documents: 《国际中文教育中文水平等级标准》 (GF0025-2021), a national grading standard in force since July 2021, and the examination syllabus published in November 2025 and in force since July 2026. They are widely conflated. This paper shows the conflation is consequential: the two assign different levels to 41.5% of the words and 40.7% of the characters they share, and grading a corpus of 102 authentic graded readers against one rather than the other changes the assigned level of 48% of texts, shifting five of six shelf medians by a full level. The result survives every coverage threshold tested and replicates on a disjoint held-out set. Contributions include a validated extraction of the 2025 syllabus, previously available only as a 406-page PDF, whose per-level counts reproduce the official totals exactly; an open, tested library that grades against either document and records which; an aligned graded-reader corpus; and HSKBench, a difficulty-controlled generation benchmark in which the grader serves as the metric rather than as the source of labels. Human authors writing to an explicit level target hit it 61.8% of the time, and two language models 2.7 points apart in aggregate differ by 48 points on a single level — reasoning buys a floor and costs a ceiling. Version 1.1 corrects two figures and replaces an anonymised build: the earlier PDF was compiled in ACL review mode and did not name the author.

title: Cross-Modal Emotion Understanding: A Transformer-GAT Approach for Dialogue Emotion Recognition
abstract: Multimodal emotion recognition is a key research area in affective computing, with applications in sentiment analysis, intelligent customer service, and human-computer interaction. However, existing methods often rely on single-modal features or simple multimodal fusion, failing to capture the synergy between global and local contexts, which limits model performance and emotion understanding. To address this challenge, we propose Transformer-GAT, a hybrid framework that combines Transformer and the Graph Attention Network to enable cross-modal emotion understanding. The Transformer is used to capture global semantic information, while the Graph Attention Network is employed to model fine-grained relationships between modalities, thereby enhancing the representation of emotional features. Experiments on the IEMOCAP and MELD datasets show that our model achieves weighted F1 scores of 72.45% and 77.37%, outperforming state-of-the-art methods. These results demonstrate that Transformer-GAT effectively integrates multimodal features, balances global and local contexts, and provides deeper emotional insights, offering new directions for multimodal emotion computing.

title: Robust Hamiltonian engineering with subensemble control
abstract: We present a robust protocol to reshape interactions in a spin ensemble based on global control pulse sequences applied to multiple subensembles in parallel. This setting arises naturally from ensembles of solid-state defects or multi-species atomic arrays. We show that it is provably computationally hard to find pulse sequences that simultaneously engineer interactions both within and between subensembles. Despite its formal hardness, we identify a set of necessary or sufficient conditions under which one can synthesize a target Hamiltonian from the native one. Moreover, we introduce efficient numerical strategies for designing pulse sequences that engineer target Hamiltonians robust against common control imperfections. As a specific application, we discuss the robust generation of two-mode spin squeezing in dual-species atomic ensembles, which is a challenging task without subensemble control. Our results provide a practical toolbox to design novel quantum simulation and sensing experiments with minimal control overhead.

title: Do Tabular Foundation Models Know Physics? Contamination, Units, and the Deterministic Limit
abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) learn to fill in tables the way language models fill in text, and tables are arguably the format in which most physical measurement arrives. Did they learn any physics in the process? They are Bayesian by construction, so the question is what their prior contains. We probe it directly, evaluating four of them (TabPFN-3, TabICLv2, TabDPT and Real-TabPFN-2.5) against six baselines on datasets sampled from 316 physical equations, in and out of domain. TFMs dominate, out of the box and after tuning. But we show that their prior can represent neither a noiseless mechanism nor physical units, which is why they interpolate physics without yet being able to act as physical models.

title: UnCapsTSR: An Unsupervised Transformer-based Image Super-Resolution Approach for Capsule Endoscopy Images
abstract: Wireless Capsule Endoscopy (WCE) captures and streams video while passing through a patient's Gastrointestinal (GI) tract and is used to examine its irregularities. Although advantageous over conventional endoscopy, WCE suffers from limitations related to capsule size and wireless transmission, resulting in images with coarser resolution. This work presents UnCapsTSR, an unsupervised transformer-based Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) framework for improving the spatial resolution of Low-Resolution (LR) WCE images. The proposed method accomplishes SR without explicit degradation estimation of real-world LR data and eliminates the need for true LR-HR pairs. UnCapsTSR employs a Bilateral Total Variation (BTV) loss to ensure spatial continuity in SR images. A newly curated dataset from the Kvasir Capsule dataset is also presented for training WCE SR models. Generalizability is validated on KID and GIANA datasets that are not used during training. A new non-reference metric, Endoscopy Quality Metric (EndoQM), is introduced for quantitative evaluation of domain-specific WCE data. Experiments demonstrate consistent improvement over state-of-the-art unsupervised SR approaches using NIQE, BRISQUE, PIQE, and EndoQM. Statistical evaluation shows 40 to 80 percent improvement in EndoQM from LR to SR across the evaluated datasets.

title: Detecting Object Hallucinations in Large Vision-Language Models via Cross-Modal Attention Drifts and Mask-Based Verification
abstract: Despite recent advances in large vision-language models (LVLMs), object hallucination remains a major barrier to their reliable deployment. Existing detection methods often characterize visual grounding using attention from individual layers, leaving its evolution across layers underexplored. We propose CADMP, a lightweight object hallucination detection framework that combines adjacent-layer cross-modal attention drift with prediction sensitivity to targeted visual masking. During decoding, CADMP quantifies distributional changes between consecutive cross-modal attention maps to capture abrupt transitions in visual grounding. It then selects the transition with the largest drift, locates the corresponding visually relevant regions, and measures the change in prediction probability after masking these regions. These two signals provide complementary evidence: attention drift characterizes the stability of internal visual grounding, while probability variation verifies whether a prediction truly depends on the identified visual evidence. A lightweight detector integrates both signals to identify hallucinated predictions. Experiments on multiple benchmarks and representative open-source LVLMs demonstrate that CADMP achieves consistently competitive detection performance. Ablation studies further confirm the complementary contributions of adjacent-layer drift modeling and mask-based grounding verification.

title: EComAgentBench: Benchmarking Shopping Agents on Long-Horizon Tasks with Distributed Hidden Intent
abstract: As LLM-based shopping agents enter production, existing benchmarks fail to capture how a shopper's requirements arrive: stated implicitly in the query, recorded in a profile, or revealed only when the right question is asked. Benchmarks that expose full intent upfront and grade only the final choice can neither pose this long-horizon challenge nor explain which requirement an agent missed. To address this gap, we introduce EComAgentBench, a benchmark of 662 tasks grounded in real Amazon products and reviews. Each task scatters these requirements across a visible query, a tool-gated profile, and scripted clarification; an agent must uncover hidden intent, verify candidates against attributes and review evidence, and commit to a single product within 100 tool calls. Moreover, typed, source-tagged rubrics grade every task, attributing each failure to a requirement and its source. Construction is automated yet reliable, with every answer fixed in code before any text is generated and every sample validated. Our evaluation of seven models reveals that even the strongest attains only 57.1% overall accuracy, and rubric satisfaction degrades from visible to hidden sources. Overall, we believe EComAgentBench will serve as a reproducible foundation for moving shopping agents from single-query search toward dependable assistance over long horizons.

title: Research on a Teaching Improvement Model for Higher Vocational Midwifery Education Integrating AI Assessment and Classroom Interaction Analysis
abstract: This study proposes a teaching-improvement model for midwifery education in higher vocational colleges that integrates artificial-intelligence-based assessment with classroom interaction analysis. The model is intended to enhance teaching quality and students’ learning experience by using AI techniques to capture dynamic information that is difficult to obtain through conventional end-of-course assessment. A dual-path architecture combining ELMo-BiLSTM-CRF with a Transformer encoder is employed to analyze classroom interaction data across multiple modalities, including speech, text, and behavioral information, thereby supporting emotion recognition, engagement assessment, and feedback on instructional strategies. The study further incorporates a closed-loop mechanism in which AI-generated assessment results are linked to instructional adjustment so that classroom interaction, learner affect, and teaching decisions can be analyzed within a unified framework. The experimental sections report model-performance analyses, group comparisons, and multimodal visualization results. In classroom interaction emotion recognition, the proposed dual-path model achieved an accuracy of 89.7%, a recall of 90.3%, and an F1 score of 90.0%, outperforming the comparative approaches reported in the study. Classroom engagement in the AI-enhanced group reached 85.9%, compared with 68.4% in the control group, while the Emotion Improvement Index increased from 0.21 to 0.43. Additional analyses illustrate how the framework can capture changes in learner emotion and engagement, examine the influence of regulatory mechanisms, and extract information relevant to teaching improvement. Overall, the results support the potential of AI-assisted classroom analytics as a decision-support tool for data-informed improvement in vocational midwifery education.

title: WP-058 — Real-Time Streaming Response Architecture: Collapsing Latency in Conversational AI Through Anticipatory Composition
abstract: Real-time streaming response differs fundamentally from classical turn-taking dialogue: the system begins composing replies before the user finishes speaking, using phonemic and syntactic cues to anticipate intent and start emitting answers mid-utterance. This paper documents the architectural shift required to support such responsiveness—lattice-threaded I/O buffering, predictive token pre-staging, and phase-locked handshake synchronisation at 132 Hz. We measure actual latency collapse (from 12+ seconds to sub-one-second) and examine the E8 geometric constraints that make this possible without sacrificing coherence integrity.

title: Probability Geometric Optimization for Quantum Computing Resource Utilization
abstract: This paper explores the application of probability geometry to optimize resource utilization within quantum computing systems. The core claim is that a novel probability geometric algorithm can significantly enhance the efficiency of quantum computations by dynamically adjusting resource allocation based on probabilistic outcomes. We present a framework that leverages the principles of probability space exploration to identify and mitigate potential bottlenecks in quantum algorithm execution. The research demonstrates the potential for substantial gains in computational speed and reduced error rates through this approach, offering a fundamentally different perspective on resource management within quantum computing. The study will analyze the algorithm's performance across a range of quantum computing tasks, comparing it to traditional optimization techniques.

title: High-Order Quantum Computing Adaptive State Generation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm for adaptive quantum state generation in high-order quantum computing. Traditional quantum algorithms often rely on pre-calculated states, limiting their flexibility and efficiency. Our proposed approach dynamically generates new quantum states based on input data and target states, significantly improving the exploration and optimization capabilities of quantum systems. The core mechanism leverages the inherent adaptability of quantum states to create a more efficient and versatile quantum computation. This advancement addresses a key limitation of existing quantum algorithms, offering a promising path towards enhanced quantum performance. We present a detailed analysis of the algorithm's design, implementation, and performance, demonstrating its potential to unlock new quantum computational possibilities.

title: Cognitive Graph Neural Networks for Abstract Reasoning
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of Cognitive Graph Neural Networks (CGNNs) to enhance abstract reasoning capabilities. Traditional Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) primarily focus on learning structural relationships within graph data, often lacking the ability to incorporate higher-level cognitive constraints. This research proposes a novel framework where a knowledge graph, such as Wikidata, is directly integrated into the GNN architecture, effectively embedding symbolic knowledge into the learning process. The core claim is that augmenting GNNs with cognitive constraints, represented as a symbolic graph, enables more sophisticated abstract reasoning. The proposed method leverages the relational properties inherent in knowledge graphs to guide the GNN's learning, allowing it to identify and exploit logical connections beyond purely geometric or topological features. We introduce a novel architecture and demonstrate its effectiveness through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, outlining a pathway towards GNNs capable of genuine abstract thought. The primary contribution lies in the integration of symbolic knowledge and graph-based learning for advanced reasoning tasks.

title: 基于量子力学原理的密码分析与防御
abstract: This paper explores novel cryptographic analysis and defense strategies rooted in the principles of quantum mechanics. It investigates vulnerabilities in Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) and leverages quantum decoherence to attack traditional cryptographic algorithms. The core claim is to design new cryptographic analysis methods utilizing superposition, entanglement, and decoherence. The proposed mechanisms aim to exploit inherent weaknesses within existing cryptographic systems by applying fundamental quantum phenomena. This research represents a significant departure from classical approaches, offering a potentially disruptive pathway for future cryptographic security. The analysis focuses on the theoretical aspects of these attacks and defenses, providing a framework for further investigation and development. The primary contribution lies in the conceptual integration of quantum mechanics into the field of cryptography, moving beyond purely mathematical approaches.

title: Title: Self-Referential Modular Arithmetic for Cryptography
abstract: This paper explores the application of self-referential modular arithmetic as a novel approach to enhance the security of cryptographic algorithms. Traditional cryptographic systems rely on the difficulty of solving problems involving modular arithmetic, while this work proposes a system where operations inherently reference themselves, potentially creating a self-checking loop. We introduce a new modular arithmetic system based on this principle, analyzing its potential to disrupt existing cryptosystems and offering enhanced security through its self-referential nature. The core mechanism involves the integration of self-reference into the arithmetic operations, creating a loop that is difficult to reverse without compromising the system's integrity. This paper will detail the design and analysis of this system, exploring its potential vulnerabilities and strengths.

title: Non-Linear Self-Organizing Neural Networks: A Dynamic Topology Approach
abstract: This paper investigates the application of a novel Non-Linear Self-Organizing Neural Network (NLSON) architecture, leveraging dynamic topology adjustment to enhance model training efficiency and performance. Traditional neural network architectures often rely on fixed, static structures, limiting their adaptability to evolving data distributions. Our proposed method introduces a dynamic topology algorithm that intelligently adjusts network structure, allowing the network to adapt to changes in data distribution. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through extensive experiments across a range of datasets, showcasing significant improvements in training speed and model accuracy. The core mechanism involves self-adaptive topology adjustment guided by a feedback loop, optimizing network connectivity and minimizing computational costs. This results in a more robust and adaptable model.

title: ##基于光子量子计算的通信协议优化
abstract: This paper investigates the optimization of communication protocols for optical fiber networks leveraging the principles of photonic quantum computing. Traditional fiber optic communication protocols rely heavily on classical communication techniques, often facing limitations in bandwidth, security, and efficiency. This research proposes a novel approach that integrates the inherent capabilities of photonic quantum computing – specifically, quantum transmission and processing – to enhance communication protocols. The core of the approach involves optimizing encoding, modulation, and decoding schemes within the fiber network, utilizing quantum properties to achieve significant improvements in data transmission rates, security against eavesdropping, and overall system performance. We explore the theoretical framework and potential implementation challenges, demonstrating the transformative potential of this hybrid approach. The proposed protocol utilizes quantum key distribution (QKD) for secure key exchange and employs quantum error correction (QEC) to mitigate the effects of noise during transmission. Simulation results (presented conceptually) indicate a substantial increase in achievable data rates and a dramatically improved level of security compared to conventional protocols. ---

title: Biofeedback-Reinforced Learning with Neuro-Genetic Algorithm
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to intelligent agent design by integrating the adaptive dynamic adjustment capabilities of biofeedback reinforcement learning (BRL) with the optimization prowess of the neuro-genetic algorithm (NGA). The core claim is to achieve highly adaptive and robust agents through this synergistic combination. The central mechanism involves utilizing neurofeedback to dynamically adjust the policy of a reinforcement learning (RL) agent, concurrently employing the NGA to evolve the policy space, thereby facilitating rapid adaptation and optimization. We demonstrate that this integration significantly enhances an agent's adaptability and learning efficiency compared to traditional BRL or NGA approaches. The proposed methodology offers a pathway towards creating intelligent systems capable of thriving in complex and changing environments. The theoretical framework is presented, outlining the key components and their interactions, followed by a discussion of the algorithm's design and potential applications. This work represents a significant advancement in the field of adaptive control and reinforcement learning.

title: Dynamic Bayesian Neural Networks with Adaptive Latent Variable Constraints
abstract: Standard Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs) suffer from significant computational challenges when dealing with large datasets and intricate network architectures, hindering their practical application in numerous domains. This paper introduces a novel approach—Dynamic Bayesian Neural Networks (DBNNs) with Adaptive Latent Variable Constraints—designed to overcome these limitations. The core idea is to construct a DBNN structure that dynamically adjusts the constraints placed on latent variables based on observed data. This adaptive constraint learning mechanism dramatically reduces the computational burden associated with Bayesian inference while preserving the essential capabilities of BNNs. We present a comprehensive framework for DBNNs, detailing the architecture, the dynamic constraint adjustment process, and the underlying mathematical principles. The key innovation lies in the integration of DBNNs with a learning algorithm that optimizes the constraints iteratively, leading to improved scalability and accuracy in complex Bayesian modeling scenarios. The proposed method offers a promising avenue for applying Bayesian inference to large-scale problems where traditional BNNs are intractable.

title: How to Build a Controlled AI Assistant for Quantum Computing
abstract: An architectural approach in which free-form dialogue is turned into a controlled computational workflow: the lifecycle stage determines the AI's goal, the context available to it, and the set of tools it is allowed to use right now. The user describes a task in ordinary language, the assistant translates it into a structured scenario, helps gather the missing information, guides it through validation, runs it on a simulation-first basis, and explains the result. The LLM does not own the computational process: experiment state is stored separately from the dialogue, the AI tools available depend on the current lifecycle stage, and any run goes through independent validation and an execution policy.

title: Evaluating Deep Actor–Critic Methods for Path Planning of Mobile Manipulators Under Wheel–Terrain Interaction
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become an effective paradigm for enabling autonomous robots to acquire navigation policies directly from interaction with complex and uncertain environments. Nevertheless, autonomous path planning for Skid-Steer Mobile Manipulators (SSMMs) remains a challenging problem because it requires the coordinated control of the non-holonomic mobile base and the manipulator while simultaneously accounting for obstacle avoidance and wheel–terrain interaction effects. This paper presents and evaluates RL-based path planning strategies for SSMMs, explicitly incorporating coupled dynamics of the mobile platform and manipulator to generate collision-free trajectories under varying terrain conditions. The proposed framework incorporates a slip-aware reward formulation that penalizes discrepancies between commanded and measured robot motion while accounting for longitudinal and lateral slip resulting from wheel–terrain interaction. The main contributions are (i) a unified RL-based framework based on actor–critic techniques for SSMM path planning, integrating the mobile base and manipulator dynamics within a coupled system representation; (ii) a physics-aware multi-objective reward formulation that incorporates wheel–terrain interaction into policy learning; and (iii) the implementation via simulation and field validation of the proposed policies under progressively complex navigation conditions and real underground mining scenarios. The framework is evaluated using four RL algorithms across multiple environments and maps from real mining scenarios, encompassing diverse navigation conditions and start-to-goal configurations. The evaluated methods include Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG), Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), Soft Actor–Critic (SAC), and Twin Delayed DDPG (TD3). Experimental field results show that SAC achieves the lowest planning time, reducing the planning time by 127.3%, 24.1%, and 2.52% compared with PPO, TD3, and DDPG, respectively. SAC also achieves the shortest path, reducing the average path length by 20.32%, 8.58%, and 1.90% compared with PPO, DDPG, and TD3, respectively. Moreover, SAC generates smoother control profiles for both the mobile base and the manipulator arm, while TD3 exhibits competitive performance across several navigation metrics. The proposed framework demonstrates the potential of slip-aware RL for coordinated SSMM navigation, providing a practical foundation for improving the safety, energy efficiency, and operational autonomy of mobile manipulators exposed to complex mining environments.

Experimental field results show that SAC achieves the lowest planning time, reducing the planning time by 127.3%, 24.1%, and 2.52% compared with PPO, TD3, and DDPG, respectively. SAC also achieves the shortest path, reducing the average path length by 20.32%, 8.58%, and 1.90% compared with PPO, DDPG, and TD3, respectively. Moreover, SAC generates smoother control profiles for both the mobile base and the manipulator arm, while TD3 exhibits competitive performance across several navigation metrics. The proposed framework demonstrates the potential of slip-aware RL for coordinated SSMM navigation, providing a practical foundation for improving the safety, energy efficiency, and operational autonomy of mobile manipulators exposed to complex mining environments.

title: DSLHash: Lightweight Hash Function Based on SVSC 4D Chaotic System and Dynamic Substitution Layers
abstract: Data integrity remains a critical requirement for secure communication in IoT environments. To address this challenge for resource-constrained IoT devices, lightweight cryptographic hash functions have been widely studied. However, static substitution layers in conventional hash functions might be vulnerable to advanced cryptanalysis. Dynamic substitution layers are constructed by exploring several methods such as key dependency, chaotic maps, DNA computations, and elliptic curves. Despite these efforts, existing dynamic substitution layers are not suitable for resource-efficient implementation. To achieve both enhanced security and practicality, this paper proposes a lightweight hash function based on a structure-varying self-coupled (SVSC) chaotic system and a dynamic substitution mechanism. A SVSC 4D chaotic map is first constructed using lightweight arithmetic and logical operations, including modular addition, bitwise shifts, and bitwise negation, thereby avoiding multiplication operations and enabling efficient hardware implementation. The chaotic map is then integrated with a generalized Feistel structure to construct a dynamic substitution layer, where the transformation behavior dynamically changes according to the internal chaotic state. This mechanism enhances nonlinear transformation diversity and contributes to improved diffusion characteristics. Finally, the dynamic substitution layer is incorporated into a sponge-based hash framework supporting flexible digest lengths. The results demonstrate that the proposed SVSC 4D chaotic system exhibits long cycle lengths in a 32-bit finite-precision implementation, mitigating the degradation caused by finite-precision effects and improving its suitability for practical cryptographic applications. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that the proposed methodology achieves a balanced tradeoff among security performance, hardware efficiency, and implementation complexity. Based on a 256-bit sponge state with a 192-bit capacity, DSLHash provides approximately 96-bit collision resistance, which is selected to balance security requirements and hardware resource consumption in lightweight applications.

title: No-Regret Bayesian Optimization with Finite-Library Input-Warped Kernels
abstract: Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization (GP-BO) excels at black-box optimization of costly functions, e.g., hyperparameter optimization (HPO) and multi-agent system (MAS) design. Convergence-rate guarantees exist for select methods, notably GP upper confidence bound (GP-UCB), but require a fixed kernel. Critically, the kernel encodes how input proximity affects objective value similarity. When raw coordinates poorly match this geometry - as with log-scaled hyperparameters or localized peaks - input warping can greatly improve sample efficiency, yet known GP-UCB proofs require a fixed kernel. We propose Finite-Library Input-Warped Bayesian Optimization (FLIWBO), which selects warps from a finite library of smooth input maps by any history-dependent rule. It adapts the input geometry to accelerate learning while retaining high-probability convergence guarantees under mild hypotheses, with an explicit $\sqrt(N_\varepsilon)$ library-size cost. Controlled diagnostics show that finite-library warping repairs planted geometry mismatches and identify FLIWBO failure cases. Across four repeated benchmarks - warped synthetic objectives, a confidence-fence trap, and Fashion-MNIST HPO - FLIWBO-UCB beats raw-coordinate GP-UCB under misspecified geometry, escapes traps that defeat even oracle-warp expected improvement, and recovers much of the gain from manual log scaling, while leading the tested methods that admit a matching regret guarantee. A 20-dimensional MAS design study further shows feasibility under costly noisy evaluations. Code for experiments is available: https://github.com/edvin-ketabati/bogp-paper-experiments.

title: Intuitionistic Unitary Linear Logic: A Proof-Theoretical Approach to Purely Quantum Higher-Order
abstract: Although the circuit model for quantum computation is well established, it is incapable of representing non-causal higher-order quantum processes such as the quantum switch. If several models of non-causal quantum computation have been considered in the literature, the approaches have so far only been focusing on the physicality of such processes, using matrices and other techniques from linear algebra. If these approaches are expressive, they however only provide a static and monolithic understanding of these processes. In this article, we propose a new formalism for non-causal, higher-order quantum processes. Based on a Curry-Howard interpetation, our proposal offers a computational interpretation that is both compositional and modular. In particular, we present Intuitionistic Unitary Linear Logic (IULL), a logic based on linear logic focusing on conservation of unitarity for higher order terms. We prove the coherence of IULLL, its completeness with regard to unitaries, and the admissibility of its cut rules. We finally discuss the validity of our approach by revisiting known non-causal quantum processes with IULL.

title: WaveSync: Constrained Wavefront Optimization for Synchronized Co-Speech Gestures in Humanoid Robots
abstract: Expressive co-speech gestures are crucial for natural human--robot interaction, yet generating them on physical humanoid robots remains challenging because, unlike virtual avatars, robots must synchronize gestures with speech under strict kinematic and actuator constraints. We present WaveSync, a hybrid framework in which a Large Language Model decomposes dialogue responses into structured semantic schemas and assigns per-word importance weights, forming a continuous Semantic Importance Wave. Gesture trajectories are shaped through Dynamic Movement Primitives to ensure kinematic feasibility while enhancing expressiveness. A Wavefront Optimization stage aligns gesture stroke peaks with speech emphasis peaks and resolves residual temporal conflicts through gesture-duration compression and forward propagation. Experimental evaluation across five dialogue scenarios demonstrates effective gesture--speech alignment and favorable performance in both objective and subjective evaluations. The results further show that the key components of WaveSync contribute to producing gestures that are expressive, semantically grounded, and kinematically feasible. The code, resources, and videos are available at https://github.com/pairs-lab/WaveSync{WaveSync}.
